> One endpoint for everything you want to remember: notes, files, photos, recordings and logs are filed with their time,
> place and provenance, linked to what you already know, and kept as a temporal semantic knowledge graph you can search by
> effort (quick, standard, deep) and revisit through time.

## README.md

# AbstractNote

One endpoint for everything you want to remember. Send a sentence, a document, a photo, a
recording, a log. AbstractNote files it with its time, place and provenance, links it to what
you already know, and grows a **temporal semantic knowledge graph** of your ideas, projects,
people and decisions. You search it by effort (quick, standard, deep) and revisit it through
time: what you knew, when you learned it, and how your view changed.

AbstractNote is part of the AbstractFramework. It runs on **AbstractGateway** (sign-in, one
runtime and one notebook per user, app hosting), **AbstractRuntime** and **AbstractFlow** (the
capture and understanding workflows), **AbstractMemory** (temporal facts) and **AbstractCore**
(models, structured output, embeddings).

Status: version 0.1.0, in development. It is not published on PyPI or npm yet; you install it
from source (see [Install](#install)).

## What you get

- **Capture anywhere**: the web app, the Apple Watch app, the `abstractnote` command line, and
  agents. Attachments are de-duplicated by content; a retried send never saves a note twice.
- **Automatic filing**: a small fast model gives each note a title, a kind, topics, an urgency
  and its language, next to the time and place it was made.
- **Self-organising knowledge**: a model resolves people, projects and ideas against candidates
  that exact lookups, full-text and vectors produce. Every change is a revision you can replay,
  and every claim keeps the note it came from.
- **Remember by cue and effort**: quick (no model, under a second), standard (one synthesis with
  citations), deep (a background dossier). Then-versus-now for any person, project, idea or link.
- **Reflection**: open loops, contradictions, things that went quiet and connections you may have
  missed, surfaced as insights.
- **Imports**: Claude Code sessions, an agora hub database, Markdown trees and plain files, with
  their original dates and provenance.

## Install

AbstractNote needs Python 3.10 or later and the framework packages next to it. Until the
packages are published, install everything from source checkouts:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractsemantics -e ../abstractcore -e ../abstractruntime \
                      -e ../abstractmemory     # a checkout that has close_assertion, see below
.venv/bin/pip install -e .
.venv/bin/abstractnote --help
```

Two framework changes that AbstractNote relies on are not in released packages yet:

- **AbstractMemory `close_assertion`** (the `close-assertion` branch): closes a superseded fact in
  place. AbstractNote's first release waits for the AbstractMemory release that contains it.
- **The AbstractGateway integration** (the `abstractnote-seam` branch): binds the note tools to
  each user's notebook, serves the note read API and lists the Note app. You need it only for the
  gateway path; the headless notebook works without a gateway. The gateway must carry this seam
  (`abstractgateway.abstractnote_seam`; the first gateway release with it is named at
  AbstractNote's release): the `[gateway]` extra alone does not guarantee it, and
  `abstractnote.gateway` refuses to import into a gateway without it, with one sentence.

To run models locally on Apple silicon, add `pip install "abstractcore[apple]"` (MLX).

## Quick start

A headless notebook on this machine, no gateway and no model:

```sh
abstractnote capture "Met Dana about the LUT budget; she wants the Pareto by Friday." --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote search "LUT budget" --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote status --notebook ~/notes
```

Let a model understand the queued notes (entities, claims, tasks), then ask a question:

```sh
abstractnote process --local --notebook ~/notes --provider mlx --model mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit
abstractnote search "What does Dana want?" --effort standard --notebook ~/notes \
    --provider mlx --model mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit
```

A notebook is pinned to the embedding model that created it. Choose it on the first command
(`--embed-base-url` and `--embed-model`, for example a local LM Studio embedding model) and give
the same flags every time, or start with the built-in offline embedder and change later with
`abstractnote rebuild --reembed`. See [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md).

Through a gateway, clients start the `note-capture` and `note-recall` flows with the gateway's
runs API, and `POST /api/gateway/note/processor/ensure` creates the per-user processor that
understands notes in the background. The getting-started guide walks through a private scratch
gateway, the web app and the watch app.

## Clients

| Client | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Web app | [`web/`](web/) (`@abstractframework/note`) | Capture (a chat with attachments), Graph (entities and links through time), Remember (since you last looked, cue cards, ask by effort, then and now), Settings |
| Apple Watch app | [`watch/apple/`](watch/apple/README.md) | Note, Ask, Today, Settings; watch-only, watchOS 26 or later |
| Command line | `abstractnote` | Headless capture, search, processing, imports, rebuild, JSON output for scripts and agents |

An iPhone app is planned ([`phone/iphone/`](phone/iphone/README.md)). Agents use the same note
tools and flows, with the effort level as a parameter.

## docs/getting-started.md

# Getting started

This guide takes you from a source checkout to a working notebook in two steps: first a
**headless notebook** on your machine (no gateway, and no model until you want one), then the
**gateway path** with the web app and the Apple Watch app. For what AbstractNote is, see the
[README](../README.md); for how the parts fit, see [architecture.md](architecture.md). If a step
fails, [troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md) lists the messages you may see and their fixes.

## 1. Install from source

AbstractNote is not published on PyPI or npm yet. You need Python 3.10 or later and source
checkouts of the framework packages next to this repository (the AbstractFramework
`scripts/clone.sh` clones them side by side):

```text
abstractframework/
  abstractcore/  abstractmemory/  abstractruntime/  abstractsemantics/  abstractgateway/
  abstractnote/   <- this repository
```

AbstractMemory must include `close_assertion` (its `close-assertion` branch until the next
AbstractMemory release). From the `abstractnote` folder:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractsemantics -e ../abstractcore -e ../abstractruntime -e ../abstractmemory
.venv/bin/pip install -e .
.venv/bin/abstractnote --help
```

The examples below call `abstractnote` directly; activate the environment first
(`. .venv/bin/activate`) or prefix the commands with `.venv/bin/`.

## 2. A headless notebook in five minutes

A notebook is a directory. Every command takes `--notebook DIR` and creates the directory the
first time. Output is JSON on standard output, so you can pipe it to `jq` or read it from a
script.

### Choose the embedding model first

A notebook is **pinned to the embedding model that creates it**: the first command that opens
the notebook (a capture included) records the model, and every later command must use the same
one. You have two choices:

- **No flags**: the built-in hashing embedder. It is offline and deterministic, and it matches
  exact and near-exact wording well, but it is not a semantic model.
- **An OpenAI-compatible embedding server**, for example a local LM Studio:
  `--embed-base-url http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 --embed-model text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b`.
  Give the same two flags on every command for that notebook.

You can change models later with `abstractnote rebuild --reembed` plus the new flags; it replays
the whole notebook into fresh stores with the new vectors.

### Capture, then look

```sh
abstractnote capture "Met Dana about the LUT budget; she wants the Pareto by Friday." \
    --notebook ~/notes --at 2026-10-19T09:12:00Z --key first-note
abstractnote capture "The plan for the review" --file plan.md --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote search "LUT budget" --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote changes --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote day 2026-10-19 --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote status --notebook ~/notes
```

- `--key` is an idempotency key: sending the same key again answers `"status": "duplicate"` and
  saves nothing new.
- `--file` attaches a file (repeatable). Text, Markdown and PDF attachments are read and
  indexed; the bytes are stored once per distinct content.
- `search` at the default **quick** effort uses full-text plus vector search and no model.
- `status` shows the counts, the queue and the embedding pin.

A note captured from the command line is stored and queued at once. Its understanding (summary,
topics, entities, claims, tasks) comes from processing, below.

### Process the queue with a model

Processing runs the `note-process` flow for each queued note, with the same flows the gateway
runs. A small fast model is recommended. On Apple silicon, install the MLX extra once and use a
mixture-of-experts model such as Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (4-bit):

```sh
pip install "abstractcore[apple]"
abstractnote process --local --notebook ~/notes \
    --provider mlx --model mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit
```

`--max-items` (default 20) and `--budget-s` (default 90) bound one pass; run it again until
`status` shows an empty queue. Any provider that AbstractCore supports works with
`--provider` and `--model` (for example `lmstudio` or `ollama` with a model they serve).

### Ask a question

```sh
abstractnote search "What did Dana ask for, and did it change?" --effort standard \
    --notebook ~/notes --provider mlx --model mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit
```

`standard` expands the quick hits through the graph and writes one answer with `[nt_...]`
citations; `deep` plans several search rounds and stores a dossier as a note. See
[remembering.md](remembering.md) for the design of the effort levels.

### Import what you already have

Imports write notes at bulk priority with their original dates, so live notes are always
processed first. Count first with `--dry-run`, then import:

```sh
abstractnote import markdown ./docs --notebook ~/notes --dry-run
abstractnote import markdown ./docs --notebook ~/notes
abstractnote import files ~/Pictures/whiteboards --notebook ~/notes
```

`claude-sessions` and `agora` work the same way; see [importers.md](importers.md) and the CLI
reference in [api.md](api.md#cli).

## 3. The gateway path

Inside AbstractGateway every user gets their own notebook, the flows run as durable runs, a
processor automation drains the queue every two minutes, and the web and watch apps connect to
it. The gateway needs the AbstractNote integration, which lives on AbstractGateway's
`abstractnote-seam` branch until a gateway release contains it.

Install that checkout into the same environment. Install it editable, and do not use
AbstractNote's `[gateway]` extra yet: the extra resolves AbstractGateway from PyPI, which does
not have the integration.

```sh
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractgateway     # on the abstractnote-seam branch
```

The gateway must carry the AbstractNote seam, its `abstractgateway.abstractnote_seam` module
(the first AbstractGateway release that contains it will be named here when AbstractNote is
released). Importing `abstractnote.gateway` into a gateway without it fails at once with one
sentence ("This AbstractGateway does not carry the AbstractNote seam …"), never half-working.

To check a running gateway, ask for the note status as a signed-in account: `200` means the note
API is mounted, `404` means this gateway has no AbstractNote integration (without a token every
`/api/gateway` path answers `401`, so that tells you nothing).

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18851/api/gateway/note/status \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <alice's token>"   # 200
```

### Try it on a private scratch gateway

`scripts/hermetic_gateway.sh` starts a gateway with AbstractNote on `127.0.0.1:18851`, in a
scratch data directory, with a clean environment and a scripted stand-in model (no weights, fixed
answers), and creates two user accounts. It prints each account's token as a parameter you can
paste:

```sh
VENV=$PWD/.venv ROOT=$PWD/untracked/hermetic scripts/hermetic_gateway.sh start
# gateway: http://127.0.0.1:18851 ...
# alice:  --token <alice's token>
# bob:    --token <bob's token>
```

Create the processor and reflect automations for an account (the web app does this for you when
you open it and they are missing):

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18851/api/gateway/note/processor/ensure \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <alice's token>"
# {"processor_id": "...", "reflect_id": "...", "created": ["note-drain", "note-reflect"]}
```

Send a note through the runs API and read the answer:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18851/api/gateway/runs/start \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <alice's token>" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"bundle_id": "abstractnote", "flow_id": "note-capture", "session_id": "demo",
          "input_data": {"text": "Met Dana about the LUT budget.", "session_id": "demo",
                         "idempotency_key": "demo-1", "source": {"client": "cli"}}}'
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18851/api/gateway/runs/<run_id> -H "Authorization: Bearer <alice's token>"
# "output": {"response": "Saved as ...", "note_id": "nt_...", "status": "queued", ...}
```

Stop it with `VENV=$PWD/.venv ROOT=$PWD/untracked/hermetic scripts/hermetic_gateway.sh stop`.
The scratch directory stays until you delete it. Ports must be in the 18800-18899 range
(`PORT` and `STUB_PORT` choose others).

### The web app

The web app needs Node.js 18 or later. Against a gateway:

```sh
cd web
npm install
npm run dev -- --gateway-url http://127.0.0.1:18851
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:3006/` and sign in with an account token. To look around without a
gateway, `npm run dev:mock` serves the app with a built-in sample notebook. `npm run build`
then `npm start -- --gateway-url <url>` runs the production server on `127.0.0.1:3006`, the way
the gateway serves it at `/apps/note/`.

### The Apple Watch app

The watch app needs Xcode 27.1 with the watchOS 26.5 simulator runtime and XcodeGen.

```sh
cd watch/apple
scripts/build.sh
```

This generates the project, runs the Swift package tests, builds for the simulator and takes a
screenshot of every screen with the built-in sample notebook. Signing in to your own gateway and
installing on a paired watch are described in [watch/apple/BUILD.md](../watch/apple/BUILD.md).

### Accounts

Use a `user` account per person or device, never an admin token. Each account sees only its own
notebook; [clients.md](clients.md) explains sign-in and isolation.

## Next steps

- [api.md](api.md): every HTTP route, the note tools, the Python API and the CLI.
- [cognition.md](cognition.md): what the flows do, step by step.
- [faq.md](faq.md): limits and common questions.

## docs/architecture.md

# Architecture

AbstractNote is one endpoint for everything you want to remember. You (or an agent) send a
note, a file, a photo, a recording or a log. AbstractNote files it with its time, place and
provenance, links it to what you already know, and keeps a **temporal semantic knowledge
graph** that you can search by effort level (quick, standard, deep) and revisit through time.

This page describes the system as it is designed and built. The data model is in
[data-model.md](data-model.md), the cognitive process (flows) in [cognition.md](cognition.md),
the HTTP, Python and tool surfaces in [api.md](api.md), the clients in [clients.md](clients.md),
and the recall design in [remembering.md](remembering.md).

## Principles

1. **Gateway-first, thin clients.** Every client (web, Apple Watch, iPhone, CLI, agents) talks to
   AbstractGateway. The gateway authenticates the caller and routes the request to that user's
   own runtime and data plane. AbstractNote never runs a server of its own.
2. **One user, one runtime, one notebook.** All AbstractNote state for a user lives inside that
   user's gateway data plane. Clients never send user, tenant or runtime identifiers.
3. **Flows are the cognitive process.** How a note is received, classified, linked, and how a
   question is answered is written as AbstractFlow workflows that run on AbstractRuntime. You
   can open them in the Flow editor. Python tools do the deterministic bookkeeping (hashing,
   storage, candidate lookup, graph writes); language models do the judgement (classify,
   extract, link, decide what changed).
4. **Eventual consistency.** Capture is immediate and durable. Understanding is queued and
   processed in the background, in priority order, by small fast models. The graph converges;
   nothing is ever lost while it converges.
5. **Models link, not regular expressions.** Entity and relationship normalisation and
   de-duplication are decided by a language model from candidates that deterministic lookups
   produce (aliases, full-text, vectors). Exact hashes de-duplicate bytes; everything else is
   judged.
6. **Append-only history.** Every change to the graph is a revision caused by a note. The graph at
   any past moment is the replay of revisions up to that moment. Facts are superseded, never
   overwritten.
7. **Claims live in AbstractMemory's format.** Every claim is a temporal triple assertion in an
   AbstractMemory store owned by the notebook, so memory tooling reads it with the framework's
   contracts (`TripleQuery`, `active_at`, provenance). Agents and entities reach note knowledge
   through the note tools and flows, which carry the effort level and the citations.
8. **Humans can act on the graph.** Tasks can be closed, claims retracted, merges undone, by the
   user; each such action is a revision with its own provenance, so the history stays honest.

## Components

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Clients
        W[Web app<br/>@abstractframework/note]
        A[Apple Watch app]
        P[iPhone app<br/>planned]
        C[CLI and importers<br/>abstractnote]
        G[Agents and entities]
    end

    subgraph Gateway[AbstractGateway - one process, one plane per user]
        AUTH[Auth, sessions,<br/>per-user routing]
        RUNS[Runs API<br/>/runs/start, ledger, attachments]
        NOTEAPI[Note read API<br/>/api/gateway/note/*]
        RUNNER[Runner: ticks runs,<br/>automations]
    end

    subgraph Plane[User data plane  users/tenant/runtime/]
        FLOWS[AbstractNote flows<br/>capture, process, drain,<br/>recall, mine, reflect]
        TOOLS[Note tools<br/>plane-bound Python]
        IDX[(Note index<br/>abstractnote/note.sqlite3)]
        KG[(Claims<br/>AbstractMemory<br/>abstractnote/kg.sqlite3)]
        ART[(Artifacts and<br/>attachments)]
    end

    LLM[Language models<br/>via AbstractCore<br/>small fast model for filing,<br/>larger model for deep recall]
    EMB[Embeddings<br/>gateway embedding route]

    W --> AUTH
    A --> AUTH
    P --> AUTH
    C --> AUTH
    G --> AUTH
    AUTH --> RUNS
    AUTH --> NOTEAPI
    RUNS --> RUNNER
    RUNNER --> FLOWS
    FLOWS --> TOOLS
    FLOWS --> LLM
    TOOLS --> IDX
    TOOLS --> KG
    TOOLS --> ART
    TOOLS --> EMB
    NOTEAPI --> IDX
    NOTEAPI --> KG
```

### Clients

- **Web app** (`web/`): a browser app served by the gateway at `/apps/note/`, like the other
  framework apps. Three views: **Capture** (a chat where you send notes and attachments and get
  a filing answer), **Graph** (explore entities and relationships, scrub through time, see what
  happened on a day), and **Remember** (search by cue and effort, revisit, then-versus-now).
- **Apple Watch app** (`watch/apple/`): dictate or type a note and send it, ask a quick question,
  see what resurfaced today. Shares the gateway client conventions of the AbstractAssistant
  watch app.
- **iPhone app** (`phone/iphone/`): planned; the folder holds the plan and the shared contract.
- **CLI** (`abstractnote`): capture from a terminal, import corpora (Claude Code sessions, an
  agora hub database, folders of Markdown, files), run the processor headlessly, search. It works
  on a notebook directory; gateway client mode is not available in this version.
- **Agents and entities**: use the same recall tools and flows, with the effort level as a
  parameter, so digital users search the same memory as humans.

### Gateway

AbstractNote adds three things to a gateway that has `abstractnote` installed:

1. **Flows**: the `abstractnote` bundle (capture, process, drain, recall, mine, reflect).
   Clients start them with the ordinary runs API. See [cognition.md](cognition.md).
2. **Plane-bound tools**: when the gateway builds a user's runtime it binds the note tools to that
   user's data plane, exactly as it binds `read_skill`. The tools are auto-approved because they
   only touch the caller's own notebook.
3. **A read API** under `/api/gateway/note/*` for the interactive views (graph, timeline, quick
   search, queue status). It resolves the caller's plane through the gateway's own service lookup.
   Writes that change knowledge go through flows; the read API only performs small bookkeeping
   actions that are themselves recorded as revisions (close a task, retract a claim, undo a merge,
   acknowledge an insight, retry a failed note, archive). Attachments uploaded through the gateway
   are capped by the gateway's attachment limit (25 MB by default); larger files enter through the
   `abstractnote import files` command on the machine that holds them.

The gateway side of this integration is a small, explicit change in AbstractGateway (an app
catalog row, the tool binding, the router include). It is listed in the backlog as the
`abstractgateway` seam.

### Data plane

Everything for one user lives under `<plane>/abstractnote/`:

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `note.sqlite3` | The note index: notes, attachments, queue, entities, aliases, claims index, relations, revisions, topics, tasks, insights, settings, full-text and vector indexes. Rebuildable from notes plus revisions. |
| `kg.sqlite3` | The AbstractMemory `SQLiteTripleStore` holding every claim as a temporal `TripleAssertion` (plus a journal). Readable with AbstractMemory's own contracts; private to the notebook. |
| `blobs/<sha256[:2]>/<sha256>` | De-duplicated attachment bytes (original files, images, audio). |
| `extracted/<sha256>.txt` | Text extracted from attachments (documents, transcripts, image descriptions). |

Why two stores: AbstractMemory models facts (subject, predicate, object, time, provenance) and is
shared with the rest of the framework. The note index models what AbstractMemory does not
(raw notes and bytes, the queue, entity records with aliases, relation statistics, revisions,
tasks, insights) and serves interactive queries in milliseconds. The revision log is the
authoritative history; both stores can be rebuilt from notes and revisions.

## Request lifecycle

### Capturing a note

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant GW as Gateway
    participant Capture as note-capture flow
    participant Tools as Note tools
    participant LLM as Small model

    Client->>GW: POST /attachments/upload (optional)
    Client->>GW: POST /runs/start note-capture {text, context.attachments, occurred_at, location}
    GW->>Capture: tick
    Capture->>Tools: note_capture(...)  hash, store, dedup, enqueue
    Tools-->>Capture: note_id, status, similar notes
    Capture->>LLM: quick filing (kind, title, topics, urgency)
    LLM-->>Capture: structured answer
    Capture->>Tools: note_file(note_id, filing)  sets priority
    Capture-->>GW: answer_user "Saved as idea 'X'. Related: A, B."
    alt process_inline
        Capture->>Capture: subflow note-process (extract, link, revise)
    end
    Capture-->>GW: on_flow_end {response, note_id, status}
    GW-->>Client: run completed, output.response
```

### Understanding a note (background)

The **processor** is an automation per user that runs the `note-drain` flow on a schedule and on
demand. Each run leases the highest-priority queued notes and runs `note-process` for each:
look at existing knowledge (context packet), extract mentions and claims with a structured
schema, resolve each mention against candidates, let the model adjudicate (same entity, new
entity, merge, and whether a claim restates, refines or contradicts an earlier one), then apply
the revision to the index and the triple store. Failures are recorded on the note and retried
with backoff; after three failures the note is marked for the user to see.

### Remembering

- **Since you last looked** (read API): the default screen for humans and agents: what changed
  in the notebook since a cursor (new entities, superseded claims, closed loops, failed notes).
- **Quick** (read API, under a second): full-text plus vector search over notes, entities and
  claims, grouped by entity and time.
- **Standard** (`note-recall` flow, seconds): quick retrieval, graph expansion around the hits at
  the requested moment, one synthesis by a model with citations and a then-versus-now note.
- **Deep** (`note-mine` flow, minutes, background): the model plans sub-questions, searches across
  time slices, compares stances, and writes a dossier that is stored as an insight note with
  provenance, so the result itself becomes searchable.

The `note-reflect` flow runs on a schedule and surfaces open loops, contradictions, stale but
related material, and connections you may have missed, as insights.

## Dependencies and boundaries

| Package | Used for | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| AbstractGateway | auth, per-user planes, runs, attachments, automations, app hosting | AbstractNote adds flows, tools, a router; it never bypasses gateway auth |
| AbstractRuntime | durable runs, VisualFlow compiler and executor, effect handlers, tool executor | flows use only catalog node types |
| AbstractFlow | authoring format, node catalog, editor | flows are importable and editable |
| AbstractMemory | `SQLiteTripleStore`, `TripleAssertion`, `TripleQuery`, `SQLiteJournal`, embedders | library use, plus one additive store method (`close_assertion`) that closes a superseded assertion in place |
| AbstractSemantics | predicate and entity-type registry for claims | predicates outside the registry are written in the `ex:` namespace |
| AbstractCore | model calls with structured output, embeddings, media text extraction | per-node provider and model pins |
| AbstractUIC | ui-kit, panel-chat, app-server for the web app | registry packages, semver ranges |

## Related documents

- [data-model.md](data-model.md): notes, entities, claims, revisions, time and de-duplication.
- [cognition.md](cognition.md): the flows, the queue, the prompts and schemas.
- [api.md](api.md): HTTP read API, Python API, tools, CLI.
- [clients.md](clients.md): web app, Apple Watch, iPhone plan, sign-in and isolation.
- [remembering.md](remembering.md): how recall is designed for humans and agents.
- [importers.md](importers.md): turning existing corpora into notes.
- ADRs in [adr/](adr/README.md); work items in [backlog/overview.md](backlog/overview.md).

## docs/api.md

# API

AbstractNote has four surfaces: the gateway runs API (start flows), the note read API (served by
the gateway when `abstractnote` is installed), the note tools (callable from any flow or agent in
the user's runtime), and the Python library and CLI. All HTTP paths are under the gateway's
`/api/gateway` prefix and use the gateway's authentication; the caller's identity selects the
notebook. Clients never send user, tenant or runtime identifiers.

## Starting flows (gateway runs API)

Capture a note:

```http
POST /api/gateway/runs/start
{
  "bundle_id": "abstractnote", "flow_id": "note-capture",
  "session_id": "<client session id>",
  "input_data": {
    "text": "Met Dana about the LUT budget; she wants the Pareto by Friday.",
    "title": null,
    "occurred_at": "2026-10-19T09:12:00Z",
    "location": {"lat": 48.85, "lon": 2.35, "label": "Paris"},
    "source": {"client": "watch"},
    "idempotency_key": "<client uuid per capture>",
    "priority": null,
    "process_inline": false,
    "context": {"attachments": [{"$artifact": "<id from /attachments/upload>"}]}
  }
}
```

Response: `{"run_id": "..."}`. Read the answer from `GET /runs/{run_id}` when `status` is
`completed` (`output.response`, `output.note_id`, `output.status`), or follow
`GET /runs/{run_id}/ledger/stream` and show the `answer_user` message as soon as it appears.

Attachments go through `POST /api/gateway/attachments/upload` first (25 MB per file by default,
the gateway's limit); larger files are imported with `abstractnote import files` on the machine
that holds them.

Ask a question:

```http
POST /api/gateway/runs/start
{"bundle_id": "abstractnote", "flow_id": "note-recall", "session_id": "<id>",
 "input_data": {"question": "What did I decide about the LUT budget, and did it change?",
                "effort": "standard", "as_of": null, "since": null, "until": null}}
```

Output: `{response, answer, evidence: [{note_id, title, occurred_at, excerpt}], evolution:
{earliest, latest, turning_points: [...]}, open_loops: [...], follow_ups: [...], dossier_note_id?,
hits, effort}` (`hits` is the quick search the answer started from).
`response` is the answer text, so chat clients using the `abstractcode.agent.v1` contract
(`prompt` in, `output.response` out) work unchanged: `prompt` is accepted as an alias of `question`.

Run the processor now: `POST /api/gateway/automations/{processor_id}/commands
{"command_id": "<uuid>", "type": "automation.run_now"}` (the id comes from `GET /api/gateway/note/status`;
a `409 automation_busy` answer means a drain is already running).

Every run start also carries `input_data.session_id` equal to the request's `session_id` (the gateway
does not forward the run's session to the flow). Run errors appear in `output` as text starting with
`Runtime error: `; clients strip that prefix before showing the sentence.

## Note read API

Served by `abstractnote.gateway.router` and mounted by the gateway. Reads are available to any
signed-in principal for their own notebook. The few write actions are bookkeeping, not knowledge.

| Method and path | Purpose | Main parameters |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /note/status` | notebook health: counts, queue state, processor and reflect automation ids, model settings, store versions, embedding pin | |
| `GET /note/changes` | since you last looked: new notes, new entities, superseded claims, closed loops, failed notes, insights since a cursor; the default screen for humans and the first call for agents | `since (cursor or ISO), limit, as_received` |
| `GET /note/overview` | the landing data: recent notes, active entities, unacknowledged insights, today's resurfacing, activity sparkline | `days` |
| `GET /note/notes` | list notes | `q, since, until, kind, topic, entity, status, cursor, limit` |
| `GET /note/notes/{note_id}` | a note with attachments, revision, claims, linked entities, revisits | |
| `GET /note/notes/{note_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}` | attachment bytes (streams the blob) | |
| `GET /note/search` | quick recall (full-text plus vector), grouped | `q, since, until, kinds, entities, topics, limit` |
| `GET /note/entities` | list or search entities (entries merged into another are left out unless `include_merged=true`; each item carries `merged_into`) | `q, kind, sort=recent|frequent|name, cursor, limit, include_merged` |
| `GET /note/entities/{entity_id}` | entity card as of a moment: name, aliases, summary history, beliefs at `at`, relations, notes, open tasks (a merged id answers with the surviving entity and `resolved_from`); with `as_merged=true`, the entry's own record instead, not followed to the survivor | `at, as_received, as_merged` |
| `GET /note/entities/{entity_id}/timeline` | claims and notes about the entity in history order, with supersessions | `since, until` |
| `GET /note/entities/{entity_id}/then-now` | the earliest and latest summaries and the turning points (cached synthesis) | |
| `GET /note/relations/{a}/{b}` | the relationship between two entities through time: claims in history order, supersessions, then-versus-now of the link | `since, until` |
| `GET /note/claims/{claim_id}` | why do I believe this: the claim, the claims it superseded or was superseded by, the notes and attachment excerpts behind it | |
| `POST /note/claims/{claim_id}/retract` | user action: retract a claim (a revision with the account as source) | `reason` |
| `POST /note/tasks/{task_id}/close` | user action: close an open loop | `note?` |
| `POST /note/entities/{entity_id}/unmerge` | user action: undo a merge | `from_id, reason` |
| `GET /note/review` | to review: matches the notebook proposed or made on its own and disagreements it kept, each with why, the two sides, the notes behind them and the actions you can take | `limit` |
| `POST /note/review/{review_id}/confirm` | user action: confirm a proposed match (a close match becomes a merge; a merge is kept) | |

The review list (`GET /note/review`) is built from stored records only, never from reading text. Each item has a
`kind` and the rule that put it there (`why`):

| `kind` | `why` | What it is | `actions` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `close_match` | `unsure_match` | processing could not tell whether a name is an existing entity, so it created a new entry and recorded a `skos:closeMatch` claim to the candidate (listed while that claim is active and the two are still separate) | `confirm` (merge the new entry into the candidate and supersede the close match), `keep_apart` (retract the close-match claim) |
| `merge` | `merged_by_model` | processing joined two entries on its own and the merge is still in force (merges you confirmed here are never listed) | `confirm` (keep it: the item leaves the list), `unmerge` |
| `contradiction` | `disputed_pair` | a note contradicted an earlier statement and both were kept, marked disputed | `retract` either side (the item leaves the list when one side is no longer active); `confirm` is refused with 400 |

Each action is `{action, method, path, body}` with `path` under `/api/gateway`; a `null` in `body` is for the
person to fill (the reason of a retraction). `confirm` records a user-action revision with `action = match.confirm`
and `target` = the review id, with the account from the signed-in principal; confirming an item that is not waiting
for review is `404`.

A user action's revision carries `source = {account, client}`: `account` is the signed-in
principal; `client` is `web` when the request came through the Note web app's proxy (which marks
what it relays with `X-AbstractFramework-App-Proxy: abstractnote`) and `api` otherwise. Request
bodies cannot set it (an unknown field such as `client` is refused with 422).
| `GET /note/cues` | cue cards: a few reflect-generated prompts you can answer by adding a note (a person gone quiet, a decision that aged, a task mentioned often and never closed) | `limit` |
| `GET /note/graph` | nodes and edges for the explorer | `focus (entity ids), at, as_received, depth (1..3), since, until, kinds, min_count, limit` |
| `GET /note/timeline` | activity per bucket: notes, revisions, new entities, superseded claims | `since, until, granularity=day|week|month` |
| `GET /note/day/{YYYY-MM-DD}` | what happened on a day: notes, revisions with summaries, entities touched | `tz, as_received` |
| `GET /note/revisions` | revision feed | `since, until, entity, cursor, limit` |
| `GET /note/topics` | topics with counts and date ranges | |
| `GET /note/tasks` | open loops | `status, entity, limit` |
| `GET /note/insights` | insights | `kind, acked, limit` |
| `POST /note/insights/{id}/ack` | acknowledge an insight | |
| `GET /note/queue` | queue summary, failed notes with errors, and the processor's throughput (`processor: {max_items, interval}`) | `limit` |
| `POST /note/queue/{note_id}/retry` | re-queue a failed note | |
| `POST /note/notes/{note_id}/archive` | archive a note (never delete) | |
| `GET /note/settings` and `PUT /note/settings` | per-notebook settings: filing model, answering model, reflect schedule, processor schedule (`{every, max_items}`, default `2m` and 20; `max_items` 1 to 200), inline processing default; the automations take them when `processor/ensure` creates them | |
| `POST /note/processor/ensure` | create the processor and reflect automations if missing; returns their ids | |

Three dates (data-model.md "Time"): `at` asks what was true or known as of a moment of history (the
authored and valid dates); `as_received` (ISO) asks what the archive held on a date: only the notes received
by then and what they caused, leaving out material imported later even when it was written earlier. They
compose (`at` and `as_received` together: the graph as of T, from what the archive held on R). With
`as_received`, the graph, the entity card and the day answer carry `as_received` (normalised); `/changes` keeps
its pinned keys. An entity the archive did not hold yet is `400` ("That entity was not in your notebook yet on
that date."), as is a date that cannot be read.

Response envelopes are plain JSON objects; every list (`/notes`, `/entities`, `/revisions`,
`/tasks`, `/cues`, `/topics`, `/insights`, `/review`) returns `{items, next_cursor}`, with `next_cursor` null
when there is no further page (the last five never page; `limit` bounds them). Times are ISO
8601 UTC. Errors use the gateway's error shape, `{"detail": "<one sentence>"}`: `401` without a
valid sign-in, `404` for an id that is not in the caller's notebook, `400` for bad input, `501`
for a read the installed `abstractnote` does not provide.

Pinned response shapes (clients decode these strictly; absent lists mean empty):

| Endpoint | Shape |
|---|---|
| `GET /note/changes` | `{cursor, notes: [NoteRef], entities: [{entity_id, name, kind, first_seen}], superseded_claims: [{claim_id, kind, text, superseded_by, note_id}], closed_loops: [{task_id, text, closed_at}], failed_notes: [{note_id, title, error}], insights: [Insight]}` |
| `superseded_claims[]` | `kind` is `superseded` (a later note replaced the claim; `superseded_by` is the new claim's id) or `retracted` (withdrawn by a note or by you; `superseded_by` is null); `text` is the claim in plain words built from entity names and the predicate's label ("Dana works at Acme"), never ids or vocabulary terms |
| `NoteRef` | `{note_id, title, kind, occurred_at, excerpt}` |
| `Insight` | `{note_id, title, body, insight_kind, occurred_at, acked_at, evidence_note_ids, entity_ids}` |
| `GET /note/overview` | `{recent: [NoteRef], entities: [{entity_id, name, kind, note_count, last_seen}], insights: [Insight], resurfacing: [NoteRef], activity: [{day, notes, revisions}]}` |
| `GET /note/cues` | `{items: [{cue_id, text, kind, subject: {kind, id, title}, evidence_note_ids, entity_ids}]}` (cues are insight notes; `cue_id` is the note id; `evidence_note_ids` and `entity_ids` are the insight's own: the notes it rests on and the entities it is about) |
| `GET /note/tasks` | `{items: [{task_id, note_id, text, status, due, closed_at}]}` |
| `GET /note/notes/{id}` | `{note_id, title, text, kind, occurred_at, received_at, status, topics, summary, source, location, attachments: [...], revision: {...} or null, entities: [...], claims: [...], revisits: [NoteRef], insight: {kind, evidence_note_ids, entity_ids, acked_at} or null}` (`insight` is set on an insight note, `kind` being its `insight_kind`, and null on every other note) |
| `GET /note/review` | `{items: [{review_id, kind, why, reason, at, sides: [ReviewSide], evidence_note_ids, actions: [{action, method, path, body}]}], next_cursor}` (newest first; `kind` `close_match`, `merge` or `contradiction`; `why` the rule; `reason` the processor's stated reason for a merge, else null; `at` when the notebook recorded it; `evidence_note_ids` starts with the note that raised it; `next_cursor` is always null) |
| `ReviewSide` | `{type, id, name, kind, note_ids}` (`type` `entity`: `name` its display name, `kind` its entity kind, `note_ids` its newest notes; `type` `claim`: `name` the statement in plain words, `kind` null, `note_ids` the note it came from) |
| `POST /note/review/{id}/confirm` | the revision result (`{revision_id, summary, entities_merged, ...}`) plus `review_id` |
| `GET /note/entities/{id}?as_merged=true` | `{entity_id, kind, name, aliases, summary, first_seen, last_seen, note_count, merged_into, merged_at, merge: {revision_id, at, recorded_at, reason, summary, note_id} or null, notes: [NoteRef]}` (the entry's own name, aliases, summary and notes; `merge` is the revision that joined it into `merged_into`, null when it is not merged; `at` is refused with 400) |
| `GET /note/queue` | `{stats: {queued, processing, failed, by_priority, oldest_enqueued_at}, failed: [{note_id, title, occurred_at, last_error, failed_at, failures}], waiting: [{note_id, title, occurred_at, priority, state, attempts, next_attempt_at}], automations: {processor_id, reflect_id}, processor: {max_items, interval}}` (`processor` is what the processor automation was created with while it exists, otherwise the `processor_schedule` setting it will be created with; `interval` is a duration such as `2m`) |
| `note-capture` output | `{response, note_id, status, revision_summary?}` |
| `note-recall` output | `{response, answer, evidence: [NoteRef], evolution, open_loops, follow_ups, dossier_note_id?, hits, effort}` |

Linking a new note to a subject: clients may send `input_data.context.about = {kind: insight|task|cue|entity|note, id, title}` on `note-capture`; `note_capture` records it and the revision links the note to that subject (`dcterms:references`), so answering a cue or commenting an insight is traceable.

Saving an answer: the web app's "Save this answer" sends `input_data.context.answer = {question, evidence_note_ids}` on `note-capture`; `note_capture` files the note as kind `synthesis` (the quick filing keeps that kind), keeps the `source` as given, and links it to each evidence note in this notebook with `dcterms:references` (the same link `context.about` makes; evidence ids outside the notebook are left out with a warning).

Graph response:

```json
{"as_of": "2026-10-19T00:00:00Z",
 "nodes": [{"id": "ex:person-dana", "kind": "person", "name": "Dana", "first_seen": "...", "last_seen": "...", "note_count": 12, "summary": "..."}],
 "edges": [{"source": "ex:person-dana", "target": "ex:project-lut", "predicate": "schema:participant", "first_seen": "...", "last_seen": "...", "count": 5, "active": true}]}
```

## Note tools

Tools are Python callables registered with AbstractCore's `@tool` decorator and bound to a
notebook directory. Inside the gateway they are bound to the caller's plane when the runtime
is built; headless, `abstractnote.tools.bind(notebook_dir)` binds them to a local notebook.
Flows call them through `tool_calls` nodes; agents may list them in `allowed_tools`.

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `note_capture` | `text, idempotency_key?, title?, occurred_at?, location?, source?, priority?, attachments? ([{"$artifact": id}] inside the gateway; [{"path": ...}] only headless, inside the folder given to bind as allow_paths_under), session_id?, about?, answer? ({question, evidence_note_ids})` | `{note_id, status: new|duplicate, duplicate_of?, first_saved_at?, received_at, revisits: [{note_id, occurred_at}], similar: [{note_id, title, occurred_at, score}], topics: [...], attachments: [{attachment_id, sha256, mime, size, extracted_by, extracted_chars}], warnings: [...]}` |
| `note_file` | `note_id, title, kind, topics, urgency, language, one_line` | `{note_id, priority, status}` |
| `note_context` | `note_id, max_chars?` | `{note: {...}, sections: [...], similar_notes: [...], candidate_entities: [{entity_id, name, kind, aliases, summary, last_seen, active_claims: [...]}], open_tasks: [...], topics: [...], vocabulary: [{predicate, gloss}]}` |
| `note_resolve_candidates` | `note_id, mentions: [{ref, name, kind, aliases}]` | `{mentions: [{ref, candidates: [{entity_id, name, kind, aliases, summary, last_seen, score, matched_by}]}]}` |
| `note_apply_revision` | `note_id, extraction, linking` | `{revision_id, summary, entities_created, entities_merged, claims_added, claims_reinforced, claims_superseded, tasks_opened, tasks_closed, warnings}`; references outside the context packet are rejected into `create`/`new` with a warning |
| `note_queue_lease` | `worker_id, max_items=1` | `{items: [{note_id, priority, attempts}]}` |
| `note_queue_ack` | `note_id, outcome: ok|error, error?, revision_id?` | `{note_id, status, next_attempt_at?}` |
| `note_queue_stats` | | `{queued, processing, failed, by_priority, oldest_enqueued_at}` |
| `note_search` | `query, since?, until?, kinds?, entities?, topics?, limit=20, as_of?` | `{notes: [...], entities: [...], claims: [...], facets: {...}}` |
| `note_expand` | `note_ids, entity_ids, as_of?` | `{entities: [card...], claims_timeline: [...], relation_timelines: [...], neighbours: [...], then_now: [...]}` |
| `note_changes` | `since, limit` | the since-you-last-looked delta (same shape as `GET /note/changes`) |
| `note_entity` | `entity_id, at?` | the entity card |
| `note_timeline` | `since, until, granularity` | buckets |
| `note_open_loops`, `note_contradictions`, `note_resurface`, `note_anniversaries` | `limit, since?` | candidate lists for the reflect flow |
| `note_insight_write` | `kind, title, body, evidence_note_ids, entity_ids, run_id?` | `{note_id}` |

All tools are read-and-write on the caller's own notebook only and are auto-approved. Every
tool returns JSON-serialisable dictionaries and raises a `ValueError` with a plain sentence on
bad input; tools never print or log secrets. Inside the gateway the binding injects the plane's
artifact store and account; tools never accept filesystem paths there.

## Python API

```python
from abstractnote import Notebook

nb = Notebook.open("/path/to/plane/abstractnote")          # creates the stores when missing
note = nb.capture("Met Dana about the LUT budget", occurred_at="2026-10-19T09:12:00Z",
                  source={"client": "cli"})                 # -> CaptureResult(note_id, status, similar)
nb.queue.stats()
hits = nb.search("LUT budget", since="2026-07-01")          # quick tier, no model
card = nb.entity("ex:person-dana", at="2026-09-01T00:00:00Z")
graph = nb.graph(focus=["ex:project-lut"], at=None, depth=2)
day = nb.day("2026-09-14")
```

`Notebook.open(dir, embedder=...)` takes the embedding model the notebook is pinned to (none
needed for the built-in hashing embedder; `abstractnote.store.embeddings.openai_compat_embedder(url,
model)` for an OpenAI-compatible server). `Notebook` is also a context manager.

The note tools and the flows run headlessly too:

```python
from abstractnote.tools import bind, TOOL_NAMES
from abstractnote.flows.runner import NoteRunner

tools = bind("notes")                                      # the 18 note tools, bound to a notebook
runner = NoteRunner.local("notes", provider="mlx", model="mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit")
runner.run_capture("Met Dana about the LUT budget")        # the note-capture flow, quick filing included
runner.run_drain(max_items=20)                             # note-drain: process queued notes
runner.run_recall("What did Dana ask for?", effort="standard")
```

`Notebook` wraps the store (`abstractnote.store.NoteStore`), the AbstractMemory projection
(`abstractnote.store.kg.ClaimStore`), the queue, the embedder, and the recall helpers. The
processing steps (`abstractnote.process`) are pure functions over these objects so that the
flows, the CLI and the tests share one implementation.

## CLI

The `abstractnote` command works on a notebook directory. Output is JSON on standard output;
problems are one sentence on standard error. Exit codes: `0` done, `2` bad input, `3` a part that
is not installed or not available in this version (`abstractnote import`: `1` when some records
failed; they are listed under `errors`).

```
abstractnote capture ["text"] --notebook DIR [--file PATH ...] [--at ISO] [--title T] [--priority 0-3] [--key KEY]
abstractnote search "query" --notebook DIR [--effort quick|standard|deep] [--since ISO] [--until ISO] [--as-of ISO]
                    [--limit N] [--provider P --model M]          # a model for standard and deep
abstractnote entity ID --notebook DIR [--at ISO]
abstractnote day YYYY-MM-DD --notebook DIR [--tz ZONE]
abstractnote status --notebook DIR
abstractnote changes --notebook DIR [--since CURSOR_OR_ISO] [--limit N]
abstractnote process --local --notebook DIR --provider P --model M [--max-items 20] [--budget-s 90]
abstractnote rebuild --notebook DIR [--reembed]                  # replay revisions into fresh stores
abstractnote bundle [--out DIR]                                  # pack abstractnote@<version>.flow

abstractnote import claude-sessions DIR --notebook DIR [--exclude-session ID ...] [--author NAME]
abstractnote import agora DB_PATH --notebook DIR [--channels a,b] [--include-system] [--operators a,b]
abstractnote import markdown DIR --notebook DIR [--glob '**/*.md']
abstractnote import files PATH ... --notebook DIR
                    # every import also takes [--since ISO] [--until ISO] [--dry-run] [--embed-base-url URL --embed-model MODEL]
```

Every notebook command also takes `--embed-base-url URL --embed-model MODEL` (an OpenAI-compatible
embedding server). A notebook is pinned to its embedding model when it is created, by the first
command that opens it; later commands must give the same model, or run `rebuild --reembed` with
the new one; `abstractnote import` takes the same two flags (see
[troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md#this-notebooks-vectors-were-made-with-the-embedding-model-)).

`--gateway URL --token T` and `abstractnote processor ensure` are reserved for a gateway client
mode that is not available in this version (exit `3`); use the HTTP API above instead.

---

## docs/faq.md

# FAQ

Short answers to recurring questions. When the answer is a fix, it links to
[troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md); when it is a design question, it links to the page that
owns the topic.

## Using AbstractNote

### Do I need a gateway?

No, for a notebook on one machine: the `abstractnote` command line works on a notebook directory
with `--notebook DIR` and runs the flows locally with `process --local`
([getting-started.md](getting-started.md#2-a-headless-notebook-in-five-minutes)). Yes, for the web
app, the watch app, several users, and background processing on a schedule: those come from
AbstractGateway with the AbstractNote integration ([architecture.md](architecture.md#gateway)).

### Can the command line talk to my gateway?

Not in this version. `--gateway URL --token T` is reserved and answers "Gateway client mode is
not available in this version; run the command on the machine that holds the notebook with
--notebook DIR." (exit code 3). A gateway keeps a user's notebook in
`<data dir>/users/<tenant>/<runtime>/abstractnote` (or `<data dir>/abstractnote` without user
accounts); on that machine you can point `--notebook` at it. `abstractnote processor ensure` is
reserved the same way: use `POST /api/gateway/note/processor/ensure` or the web app.

### Why do notes I capture from the command line have no title or kind?

`abstractnote capture` stores the note directly, without a model. The quick filing step (title,
kind, topics, urgency, language) is part of the `note-capture` flow that gateway clients start.
Processing (`process --local`, or the gateway's processor) adds the summary, topics, entities,
claims and tasks. From Python, `NoteRunner.local(...).run_capture(...)` runs the whole capture
flow headlessly ([api.md](api.md#python-api)).

### Which models should I use?

A small fast model for filing and processing; the recommended one on Apple silicon is
`mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit` with `--provider mlx` (install `abstractcore[apple]`). Any
provider AbstractCore supports works. Inside a gateway the web app's Settings choose a
**filing model** (the processor) and an **answering model** (standard and deep recall, and the
reflect automation); "Default" uses the gateway's default text model.

### I changed the model in Settings. Why does processing still use the old one?

Settings are stored in the notebook and used when the processor and reflect automations are
created. Automations that already exist keep the models they were created with.

### What is the embedding pin, and can I change models?

Vectors from different embedding models cannot be compared, so a notebook records the model that
created it and refuses another one. Change models with `abstractnote rebuild --reembed` and the
new `--embed-base-url` / `--embed-model`: it replays notes and revisions into fresh stores with the
new vectors. See [troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md#this-notebook-is-pinned-to-the-embedding-model).

### Is anything ever deleted or truncated?

No. Notes are archived, never deleted (`POST /note/notes/{id}/archive`). Long notes are split
into sections for the model and merged before linking; the stored text and the full-text index
always keep the whole note. Superseded facts keep their history with a closed validity window.

### Does AbstractNote describe images and transcribe recordings?

It stores every attachment and reads text, Markdown and PDF files. Image descriptions and
transcripts need an image model and a speech model passed to the note tools
(`abstractnote.tools.bind(..., extractors={"vision": ..., "stt": ...})`); the gateway integration
does not configure them yet. Without them the note keeps the file and its details, and the capture
result carries a warning such as "Kept photo.jpg; no image model is configured to describe it."

### How large can an attachment be?

Uploads through a gateway follow the gateway's attachment limit (25 MB per file by default). Add
larger files on the machine that holds them with `abstractnote import files PATH`.

### How fast is processing?

Expect about two model calls per note. The gateway's processor handles up to 20 notes every two
minutes, one at a time per user, so a large import is understood over hours while live notes go
first (imports use the lowest priority). "Process now" in the web app starts a pass immediately.

### Can agents use my notebook?

Yes. Inside the gateway the note tools are bound to the caller's own notebook and auto-approved,
and `note-recall` also answers the `abstractcode.agent.v1` chat contract (`prompt` in,
`output.response` out). Agents should start a session with `note_changes` and cite the note ids
they rely on; see [remembering.md](remembering.md#for-agents-and-entities).

## Design questions

### Why not regular expressions for names and duplicates?

Identity and change are judged by a model from candidates; deterministic code only produces exact
hashes and candidate lists. See [ADR 0004](adr/0004-models-decide-identity-no-text-heuristics.md).

### Why two stores?

The revision log is the truth; the note index serves fast interactive reads and the AbstractMemory
store holds every claim as a temporal triple that framework tools can read. Both are projections
you can rebuild. See [data-model.md](data-model.md) and
[ADR 0003](adr/0003-revision-log-is-truth-index-and-abstractmemory-projection.md).

### Why is understanding queued instead of immediate?

Capture must never wait for a model. The queue gives priority order, retries and a visible state;
"Instant linking" in the web app processes a note right after capture when you want that. See
[ADR 0005](adr/0005-eventual-consistency-queue-and-processor-automation.md).

## Limits of this version

- Not published yet: no PyPI package, no npm package for the web app, no TestFlight or App Store
  build of the watch app. Install from source ([getting-started.md](getting-started.md)).
- The gateway integration and AbstractMemory's `close_assertion` are on branches of those
  packages until their next releases; AbstractMemory's must ship first.
- How the Apple apps store the sign-in (a protected file in the app container) is proposed and
  awaits a ruling ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-apple-client-credential-storage.md)).
- The command line works on local notebooks only (no gateway client mode).
- The iPhone app is planned, not built ([clients.md](clients.md#iphone-app-phoneiphone)).

---

## docs/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Each entry starts from what you see (a message, an exit code, a status), then gives the cause,
how to confirm it, and the fix. Setup steps are in [getting-started.md](getting-started.md), the
HTTP and CLI reference in [api.md](api.md), and short conceptual answers in [faq.md](faq.md).

The command line prints results as JSON on standard output and problems as one sentence on
standard error. Exit codes: `0` done, `2` bad input (the sentence says what to change), `3` a
part of AbstractNote that is not installed or not available in this version. `abstractnote
import` exits `1` when some records could not be imported (they are listed under `errors`).

## Notebook and embeddings

### This notebook is pinned to the embedding model

```text
This notebook is pinned to the embedding model 'abstractnote-hashing-v1-256' but the embedder given is 'text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b'; rebuild with reembed to change models.
```

- **Cause**: the notebook was created with one embedding model and the command gave another.
  `abstractnote-hashing-v1-256` is the built-in embedder used when the first command had no
  `--embed-base-url` / `--embed-model`.
- **Check**: `abstractnote status --notebook DIR` shows `embedding_pin.model_id`.
- **Fix**: give the pinned model's flags again, or move the notebook to the new model with
  `abstractnote rebuild --reembed --notebook DIR --embed-base-url URL --embed-model MODEL`.
  `status` then shows the new pin.

### This notebook's vectors were made with the embedding model ...

```text
This notebook's vectors were made with the embedding model 'text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b'; open it with that embedder ...
```

- **Cause**: the notebook is pinned to an embedding server and the command gave no
  `--embed-base-url` / `--embed-model`. The notebook then opens read-only: `status` (which shows
  `read_only` with this sentence), `entity`, `day`, `changes` and `search` work, and `search`
  matches words only and says so in its `warnings`. Commands that write or need new vectors
  (capture, processing, user actions, imports, rebuild) refuse with this sentence before writing
  anything.
- **Fix**: add the two flags with the pinned model to the command.
- **Imports**: `abstractnote import` takes the same two flags.

### Give both --embed-base-url and --embed-model

One of the two flags is missing. They always go together.

### Say which notebook with --notebook DIR

Every command except `bundle` needs `--notebook DIR`. A gateway keeps a user's notebook in
`<data dir>/users/<tenant>/<runtime>/abstractnote` (or `<data dir>/abstractnote` without user
accounts).

## Processing and models

### Give --provider and --model for the model that processes or answers

`process --local` and `search --effort standard|deep` run a model. Name it, for example
`--provider mlx --model mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit`.

### MLX dependencies not installed

```text
MLX dependencies not installed. Install with: pip install "abstractcore[apple]"
```

- **Cause**: `--provider mlx` needs the MLX engine, which is not part of the base AbstractCore
  install.
- **Fix**: `pip install "abstractcore[apple]"` in the same environment as `abstractnote` (on
  Apple silicon). On Linux with an NVIDIA or AMD GPU, use `abstractcore[gpu]`; anywhere else, use
  a provider that serves models over HTTP, such as `lmstudio` or `ollama`.

### Processing through a gateway is not available here

`abstractnote process` without `--local` (exit 3). Add `--local` with `--provider` and `--model`
to process on this machine, or use **Process now** in the web app's Settings to start the
gateway's processor.

### Gateway client mode is not available in this version

The command was given `--gateway`. Run it on the machine that holds the notebook with
`--notebook DIR`, or use the HTTP API ([api.md](api.md)).

### Creating the processor needs a gateway

`abstractnote processor ensure` (exit 3). Open the web app, which creates the processor when it
is missing, or call `POST /api/gateway/note/processor/ensure` with your account token.

### Notes stay queued

- **Check**: `abstractnote status` (or `GET /api/gateway/note/queue`) shows `queued`,
  `processing` and `failed`, and `automations.processor_id`.
- **Cause and fix**: with no `processor_id`, the processor automation does not exist yet: open
  the web app or call `processor/ensure` as above. With a processor, notes are processed up to 20 every two minutes,
  one at a time, highest priority first; imports wait behind live notes by design. Headless, run
  `process --local` again until the queue is empty.

### A note failed to process

The queue retries a failed note after one minute and then after ten minutes; the third failure
marks it `failed` with the error. "Processing stopped before it finished." means a run ended
while it held the note (the lease expired). Fix the cause the error names (most often the model
or provider), then press **Retry** in the web app's queue panel or call
`POST /api/gateway/note/queue/{note_id}/retry`.

### the generated flows are stale

```text
the generated flows are stale (note-process); run python -m abstractnote.flows.build
```

`abstractnote bundle` found that the flow JSON in the package no longer matches the generator
(you changed a prompt, a schema or the generator). Run `python -m abstractnote.flows.build` and
commit the regenerated `src/abstractnote/flows/json/*.json`; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Gateway

### Every /api/gateway/note call answers 404, or the bundle is unknown

- **Cause**: the gateway does not have AbstractNote, or it is a gateway release without the
  AbstractNote seam (`abstractgateway.abstractnote_seam`). In that environment
  `python -c "import abstractnote.gateway"` fails with one sentence that names the missing seam.
- **Fix**: install `abstractnote` and the AbstractGateway checkout with the integration in the
  gateway's own environment, then restart the gateway
  ([getting-started.md](getting-started.md#3-the-gateway-path)). A signed-in
  `GET /api/gateway/note/status` then answers `200`.

### Your notebook is not available: ...

Every note tool answers this sentence when the gateway could not bind the tools to your
notebook; the rest of the gateway keeps working. The reason follows the colon. The most common
one is an embedding pin: the notebook was first used with a different embedding route than the
one the gateway has now. Rebuild it with the gateway's model (`abstractnote rebuild --reembed`
on the notebook directory, gateway stopped), or restore the earlier embedding route.

### A capture waits for approval

The watch app says "This note waits for your OK in AbstractNote on another device."; a headless
run raises "run ... waits for approval of [...]; note tools must be auto-approved".

- **Cause**: the note tools are not in the gateway's auto-approve set, so the runtime parks the
  run on a tool-approval wait. The integration adds them; a gateway without it, or a custom
  approval policy that replaced the set, does not.
- **Fix**: run the gateway with the AbstractNote integration and its default approval policy.
  Note tools only read and write the caller's own notebook.

### 409 automation_busy, "Already running."

```json
{"detail": {"reason_code": "automation_busy", "message": "An occurrence is already running or waiting to run."}}
```

**Process now** was pressed while a processing pass is running or queued. Nothing is wrong; the
running pass continues and the next one follows on schedule.

### 413, "Attachment too large"

```text
Attachment too large (26214401 bytes > 26214400 bytes)
```

The file is over the gateway's attachment limit (25 MB per file by default). The web app refuses
it before uploading: "This file is larger than 25 MB; add it from the computer that has it with:
abstractnote import files <folder>." Import it on that machine, or raise the gateway's limit.

### Local file paths are not accepted here

```text
Local file paths are not accepted here; upload the file as an attachment instead.
```

A `note-capture` run was given `{"path": ...}` in `context.attachments`. Inside a gateway the
note tools only read files you uploaded: call `POST /api/gateway/attachments/upload` and pass
`{"$artifact": "<id>"}`. Headless, paths are accepted only inside a folder you allow
(`abstractnote.tools.bind(..., allow_paths_under=DIR)`); outside it the answer is "That file is
outside the folder this notebook may read from."

### Run errors start with "Runtime error: "

A flow that refuses its input still completes; its output is `{"success": false, "error":
"Runtime error: <sentence>"}` with no `response`. The sentence after the prefix is the cause
(for example the path refusal above). Clients strip the prefix before showing it.

### 401 Unauthorized, "You were signed out. Please sign in again."

The token or session is no longer valid (revoked, expired, or for another gateway). Sign in
again with a `user` account token or an emailed code. Admin tokens are not meant for clients.

### 404 "That note is not in your notebook."

The id belongs to another account's notebook or does not exist. Each account sees only its own
notebook, by design.

### The web app says "Your notebook cannot show this yet."

The gateway answered 501: the installed `abstractnote` lacks a read the web app asks for.
Install the same version of `abstractnote` on the gateway as the web app expects, then restart
the gateway.

## Attachments

### Kept the file, but its text could not be read

Capture results carry warnings such as "Kept photo.jpg; no image model is configured to
describe it.", "Kept the recording memo.m4a with its details; no speech model is configured to
transcribe it." or "Kept report.pdf; its text could not be read here (PDF reading is not
installed on this machine)." The file is always stored and linked to the note; only its text is
missing. Image descriptions and transcripts need the extractors described in
[faq.md](faq.md#does-abstractnote-describe-images-and-transcribe-recordings).

---

## docs/data-model.md

# Data model

This page defines the records AbstractNote keeps, how time works, how identities are assigned,
and how duplicates are handled. The Python types live in `abstractnote.model`; the SQLite schema
in `abstractnote.store.schema`; the AbstractMemory projection in `abstractnote.store.kg`.

## Overview

```mermaid
erDiagram
    NOTE ||--o{ ATTACHMENT : has
    NOTE ||--o| QUEUE_ITEM : "waits in"
    NOTE ||--o{ REVISION : causes
    REVISION ||--o{ CLAIM : adds
    REVISION ||--o{ ENTITY : "creates or changes"
    ENTITY ||--o{ ALIAS : "known as"
    CLAIM }o--|| ENTITY : subject
    CLAIM }o--o| ENTITY : object
    ENTITY ||--o{ RELATION : "linked by"
    NOTE ||--o{ TASK : mentions
    NOTE }o--o{ TOPIC : "filed under"
    INSIGHT }o--o{ NOTE : "evidenced by"
```

## Note

A note is anything you send: a sentence, a document, an image, a recording, a video, a log, a
chat turn imported from a transcript. It is the unit of provenance: every entity, claim and
revision points back to the note(s) that caused it.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `note_id` | `nt_<26 chars>` | Deterministic, base32 of a sha256. Imports: `sha256(importer, source_key)`. Live capture: `sha256(idempotency_key)` when the client sends one (clients always should; the runs API has no idempotency key of its own), otherwise `sha256(text_norm, attachment hashes, occurred_at to the minute, source.client)`. A retried request yields the same note; the same words said again on another day yield a new note that revisits the earlier one. |
| `kind` | enum | `idea`, `task`, `decision`, `fact`, `event`, `question`, `reflection`, `reference`, `log`, `conversation`, `personal`, `synthesis`, `insight`. Assigned by the quick filing step; `synthesis` and `insight` are system-authored. |
| `title` | text | Short title (model-written or taken from the source). |
| `text` | text | The note body as received (Markdown allowed). Never truncated. |
| `text_norm` | text | Whitespace-normalised, lower-cased copy used for hashing and full-text search. |
| `summary` | text | One to three sentences written by the processor. |
| `occurred_at` | ISO 8601 UTC | When the note was made or the event happened. From the client clock, the importer (message timestamp, file date, EXIF), or an explicit value. |
| `received_at` | ISO 8601 UTC | When AbstractNote stored it. |
| `processed_at` | ISO 8601 UTC or null | When the last successful revision was applied. |
| `source` | object | Provenance: `{client: web|watch|iphone|cli|agent|importer, importer?: claude-sessions|agora|markdown|files, origin: {...source-specific ids...}, author?: user id or agent name}`. |
| `location` | object or null | `{lat, lon, accuracy_m?, label?}` when the client provides one. |
| `language` | text or null | BCP-47 tag detected by the filing step. |
| `topics` | list | Categories assigned by filing and refined by processing (see Topics). |
| `priority` | int 0..3 | 3 urgent, 2 high, 1 normal, 0 bulk. |
| `status` | enum | `received`, `queued`, `processing`, `processed`, `failed`, `duplicate`, `archived`. |
| `duplicate_of` | note id or null | Set only when the same idempotency key or import source key arrives again (a retry), never for the same words on another occasion. |
| `session_id`, `run_id` | text | The gateway session and the run that captured it, when applicable. |
| `archived_at` | ISO or null | Notes are archived, never deleted. |

### Attachment

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `attachment_id` | `at_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, sha256)` |
| `sha256`, `size`, `mime`, `filename` | the bytes' identity |
| `artifact_ref` | the gateway artifact that carried it, when uploaded through the gateway |
| `blob_path` | `blobs/<sha256[:2]>/<sha256>`; stored once per distinct content across the notebook |
| `extracted_text`, `extracted_by` | text derived from the bytes (document text, transcript, image description, log excerpt, media metadata) and which extractor produced it (`plain`, `markdown`, `pdf`, `vision:<model>`, `stt:<model>`, `media-metadata`, `none`). Audio and video with a speech track are transcribed when a speech model is configured; otherwise, and for music, the filing keeps the metadata (filename, duration, tags) and the capture answer says so plainly. |

Two notes that attach the same file share one blob; the second attachment records the
relation `same_bytes_as` so the graph shows that the file came back.

## Entity

An entity is a thing the notes talk about: a person, an organisation, a project, a concept, a
place, an event, an artifact (a document, a dataset, a repository), a piece of software, or a
generic thing.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `entity_id` | `ex:<kind>-<slug>` following AbstractFramework ADR 0025. A collision with a different entity of the same kind appends `-2`, `-3`. Ids are never reused. |
| `kind` | `person`, `org`, `project`, `concept`, `place`, `event`, `artifact`, `software`, `thing` |
| `name` | preferred display name (case preserved) |
| `aliases` | other names seen in notes, case preserved; matching is case-folded |
| `summary` | one model-written sentence saying what the notebook knows about it, rewritten when a note tells something new (each revision kept) |
| `first_seen`, `last_seen` | `occurred_at` of the first and latest note mentioning it |
| `note_count` | number of notes that mention it |
| `merged_into` | set when the model decided this entity is the same as another; the record stays so old links still resolve |
| `embedding` | vector of `name + aliases + summary`, refreshed when the summary changes |

Entities are created only by revisions. The id is minted from the name chosen by the model at
creation time; later renames add aliases and may change `name`, never the id.

## Claim

A claim is one statement with time and provenance. Claims are the edges and attributes of the
graph.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `claim_id` | `cl_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, subject, predicate, object)`; predicate CURIEs keep their case in the index |
| `subject_id` | entity id |
| `predicate` | a CURIE from the AbstractSemantics registry when one fits (`schema:knowsAbout`, `schema:participant`, `skos:related`, `dcterms:references`, `cito:disagreesWith`, ...), otherwise `ex:<snake_case>` |
| `object_id` or `object_literal` | an entity, or a literal value (text, number, date) |
| `certainty` | `stated`, `probable`, `possible`, `reported`, `disputed` (tokens, not numbers) |
| `stance` | `assert`, `revise`, `retract`: what the note does to earlier knowledge |
| `observed_at` | the note's `occurred_at` |
| `valid_from`, `valid_until` | the validity window; `valid_from` defaults to `observed_at` for state claims and is null for timeless facts; `valid_until` is set when a later note supersedes or retracts the claim, and equals `valid_from` when you retract it ("never true") |
| `status` | `active`, `superseded`, `retracted` |
| `superseded_by` | the claim that replaced it |
| `evidence` | the verbatim excerpt of the note that supports the claim |
| `note_id`, `revision_id` | provenance |
| `assertion_id` | the id of the same claim in the AbstractMemory store (equals `claim_id`) |

### Relation

A relation is a derived, fast-to-read summary of all claims between two entities:
`(subject_id, object_id, predicate) -> first_seen, last_seen, count, active_claim_ids`. The graph
view reads relations. The **relation timeline** (`/note/relations/{a}/{b}`) is first-class: all
claims between two entities in history order, with supersessions and a then-versus-now of the
relationship, so the evolution of a link is as visible as the evolution of a node.

## Revision

A revision is the append-only record of what one processed note did to the graph. It is the
authoritative history: replaying revisions in order rebuilds entities, claims, relations, topics
and tasks.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `revision_id` | `rv_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, attempt)`; user actions use `(action, target, occurred_at)` |
| `note_id` | the cause (null for a user action; then `source` names the client and account) |
| `applied_index`, `applied_kg` | flags set after each projection commits; recovery replays revisions whose flags are not both set (idempotent thanks to deterministic ids) |
| `at` | the note's `occurred_at` (history time) |
| `recorded_at` | when the processor applied it (system time) |
| `run_id` | the processing run (ledger) |
| `ops` | ordered list of operations |
| `summary` | one sentence written by the processor ("Linked the LUT budget decision to Castor; superseded the earlier plan.") |

Operations:

| op | payload |
|---|---|
| `entity.create` | `{entity_id, kind, name, aliases, summary}` |
| `entity.alias` | `{entity_id, alias}` |
| `entity.rename` | `{entity_id, name, previous}` |
| `entity.summary` | `{entity_id, summary, previous}` |
| `entity.merge` | `{from_id, into_id, reason}` |
| `claim.add` | the claim |
| `claim.supersede` | `{claim_id, by_claim_id, reason, valid_until}` |
| `claim.retract` | `{claim_id, reason, valid_until?}` (without `valid_until`, the window closes at the revision's time) |
| `claim.reinforce` | `{claim_id, note_id}` (the same statement seen again) |
| `topic.assign` | `{note_id, topic}` |
| `task.open` / `task.close` / `task.drop` | `{task_id, text, due?, by_note_id?}` |
| `entity.unmerge` | `{entity_id, from_id, reason}` (a user action; re-points the claims that came from `from_id`) |
| `entity.mention` | `{entity_id, note_id}` (the note talks about the entity; drives `note_count`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`) |
| `note.summary` | `{note_id, summary, kind, language}` |

User actions (`close a task`, `retract a claim`, `undo a merge`, `confirm a match`) produce revisions with
`source = {client, account}` and no note; they are the human side of an actionable graph. Through
the gateway, `account` is the signed-in user and `client` is `web` (the Note web app) or `api`
(any other caller), decided by the server, never by the request body.

Confirming a match from the review list (`POST /note/review/{id}/confirm`) is a revision with `action =
match.confirm` and `target` = the review id: for a close match (an `unsure` decision, recorded as a `skos:closeMatch`
claim from the new entry to the candidate) its ops are `entity.merge` (the new entry into the candidate) and
`claim.supersede` of the close-match claim; for a merge the processor made it has no ops and only records that you
keep it. Revisions are the truth, so a rebuild keeps what you confirmed.

Reversibility: a merge keeps both records and can be undone by a later revision that re-points
claims; a supersession keeps the old claim with its window closed.

## Topic

A topic is a lightweight category (`#lut`, `#release`, `#family`). The filing step chooses from
existing topics first and proposes new ones sparingly; the processor may refine. Topics are
flat; entities carry the structure.

## Task

Open loops extracted from notes: `{task_id, note_id, text, status open|done|dropped, due?,
closed_by_note_id?}`; `task_id` is `tk_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, normalised text)`. A later note that reports the task done closes it with a `task.close` op,
decided by the model during processing.

## Insight

System-authored notes with `kind = insight` or `synthesis`: dossiers from deep recall and the
findings of the reflect flow (open loops, contradictions, resurfaced material, connections).
They carry `evidence_note_ids`, `entity_ids`, `insight_kind` (`warning`, `reminder`,
`connection`, `contradiction`, `evolution`, `dossier`, `cue`) and `acked_at`. Cue cards are the
unacknowledged insights other than dossiers, newest first.

## Time

AbstractNote is bitemporal, and every note carries three dates that answer three different questions:

| Date | Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Authored (history time) | `occurred_at`, `claim.observed_at`, `revision.at` | "When was this written or did it happen?" "What did the graph look like on day X?" |
| Valid | `claim.valid_from`, `claim.valid_until` | "What did I believe about X at time T?" |
| Archive-accepted (system time) | `received_at` (and `processed_at`, `revision.recorded_at`) | "What did my archive hold on date R?" "What has the processor done since I last looked?" |

The axes are independent: an import received today can hold notes authored years ago, and a note
written in January can say something stopped being true in March.

Rules:

- The archive **as received at R** (`as_received=R` on `GET /note/graph`, `GET /note/entities/{id}`,
  `GET /note/changes` and `GET /note/day/{date}`) = only the notes with `received_at <= R`, so material
  imported later is left out even when it was authored earlier. What derives from notes follows them: a
  revision belongs when the note that caused it was received by R (a user action without a note: when it was
