  recorded by R); entities exist when such a revision created them or such a note mentions them; merges,
  names, aliases, summaries and the closing of claims count only when their revision belongs, so a claim a
  later note superseded reads as it stood before. `at` and `as_received` compose: "the graph as of T, from
  what the archive held on R".
- The graph **as of T** = entities first seen at or before T (their creating revision's `at`, or an
  earlier note that mentions them when notes are processed out of history order), not merged away
  by T; edges from claims with `observed_at <= T`.
- **Beliefs at T** = claims with `valid_from <= T` and (`valid_until` is null or `> T`).
- Supersession sets `valid_until` of the old claim to the `occurred_at` of the superseding note;
  so does a note whose stance is `retract`.
- A retraction you make (`POST /note/claims/{id}/retract`) says the claim was never true: its
  status becomes `retracted` and `valid_until = valid_from` (its `observed_at` when it has no
  start), an empty window, never the moment you said so. Retracted claims are never beliefs.
- Importers set `occurred_at` from the source (message timestamp, commit date, file date);
  `received_at` is always the ingest time, so an import is visible as a system-time event while
  history stays truthful.
- Explicit time references inside a note ("last Tuesday", "in 2024") are extracted as claims with
  literal dates when the model can resolve them from the note's own `occurred_at`; they never
  move the note itself.

## Identity and de-duplication

| Level | Mechanism | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Bytes | `sha256` of attachment content | one blob per content; later attachments link to it |
| Retry | same idempotency key (live) or source key (import) | same `note_id`, status `duplicate`, nothing else written |
| Same words again | exact `text_norm` hash equal to an earlier note | a new note; the earlier one is the strongest `ex:revisits` candidate; the answer says "you noted this on <date>" |
| Near-duplicate note | vector cosine over note embeddings, threshold 0.92 | kept as a distinct note, linked with `ex:revisits` to the earlier one: a revisit is a signal, not noise |
| Entity | candidates from alias match (case-folded), full-text on name and aliases, vector k-nearest on entity embeddings; the model decides `same`, `different`, `unsure` per mention and may propose a merge of two existing entities | `entity.create`, `entity.alias`, `entity.merge` ops |
| Claim | same `(subject, predicate, object)` after resolution | `claim.reinforce` instead of a new claim |
| Conflicting claim | same `(subject, predicate)` with a different object and the model marks the predicate single-valued, or the note's stance is `revise` or `retract` | `claim.supersede` or `claim.retract` with reason; history kept |

No regular-expression or keyword heuristics decide identity. Deterministic steps only produce
candidates and exact-hash matches.

## AbstractMemory projection

Every claim is written to the AbstractMemory store as a `TripleAssertion`:

| TripleAssertion field | Value |
|---|---|
| `assertion_id` | `claim_id` |
| `subject`, `predicate`, `object` | entity ids and predicate CURIE; literal objects marked with `attributes.literal = true` so case is preserved |
| `scope`, `owner_id` | `global`, `abstractnote` |
| `observed_at` | the claim's `observed_at` (note time) |
| `valid_from`, `valid_until` | the claim's window |
| `confidence` | mapped from certainty: stated 0.9, probable 0.7, possible 0.5, reported 0.6, disputed 0.3 |
| `provenance` | `{source: "abstractnote", note_id, revision_id, run_id, evidence_quote, recorded_at}` |
| `attributes` | `{subject_type, object_type, certainty, stance, literal?, evidence_quote?, abstractnote_kind}` (`abstractnote_kind` is `claim`, `name`, `alias` or `same_as`) |

Entity names and aliases are written as `(entity_id, schema:name, "Name")` and
`(entity_id, skos:altLabel, "Alias")`; merges as `(from_id, schema:sameAs, into_id)`. Supersession
closes the old assertion in place with `close_assertion(assertion_id, valid_until)`, an additive
AbstractMemory store method introduced for this purpose (it updates `valid_until` only when it is
still open and leaves everything else untouched), and records a journal
`ClosureRecord(kind="supersede")` so both `TripleQuery(active_at=...)` and ranked retrieval agree
with the note index. AbstractMemory lowercases subjects, predicates and objects that are not
literals; the note index keeps the original case, and every AbstractMemory query from AbstractNote
passes `owner_id="abstractnote"`.

Write order for one revision: the revision row (intent) first, then the index projection (one
transaction that also sets `applied_index`), then the AbstractMemory projection, then `applied_kg`.
A revision whose index projection raises is set aside (nothing applied) instead of replayed. Embeddings are computed once in the
note index and handed to the triple store, so a rebuild never re-embeds over the network unless
`rebuild --reembed` is requested (for example after the embedding model changed; the pin is shown
by `GET /note/status`).

Store: `SQLiteTripleStore` at `<plane>/abstractnote/kg.sqlite3` with the notebook's embedder
(the gateway's embedding route inside a gateway; headless, the OpenAI-compatible model given on
the command line or the built-in hashing embedder; vectors are pinned to that embedding space and
handed over from the note index) and a `SQLiteJournal` in the same file (tables `memj_*`). A
notebook opened without the embedder it is pinned to opens read-only: reads and word-only search
work, and anything that would write or embed refuses with a plain sentence. A retraction (user
action or a note's `retract` stance) closes the assertion
the same way with `ClosureRecord(kind="retract")`; an undone merge closes its `schema:sameAs`.

---

## docs/cognition.md

# Cognition: the flows, the queue, the schemas

AbstractNote's thinking is written as AbstractFlow workflows (VisualFlow JSON) packaged in the
`abstractnote` bundle. They run on AbstractRuntime inside the gateway, one durable run per
invocation, and you can open every one of them in the Flow editor. Deterministic work happens in
plane-bound **note tools**; judgement happens in `llm_call` nodes with structured output.

Flow sources are generated by `abstractnote.flows.build` (a Python generator in the style of
AbstractFlow's `wf_common`) into `src/abstractnote/flows/json/*.json`; the bundle is packed by
`abstractnote bundle`. Only catalog node types are used.

## The flows

| Flow id | Interface | Started by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note-capture` | `abstractnote.capture.v1` | clients, per note | store, de-duplicate, file quickly, answer, enqueue; optionally process inline |
| `note-process` | internal subflow | `note-capture` (inline) and `note-drain` | understand one note and revise the graph |
| `note-drain` | `abstractnote.drain.v1` | the processor automation, "Process now", the CLI | lease queued notes by priority and process them one at a time |
| `note-recall` | `abstractnote.recall.v1` and `abstractcode.agent.v1` | clients, agents, per question | answer a question at the requested effort |
| `note-mine` | internal subflow | `note-recall` (deep) | multi-step mining across time; writes a dossier insight |
| `note-reflect` | `abstractnote.reflect.v1` | a scheduled automation | surface open loops, contradictions, resurfaced material, connections |

Every flow exposes `provider` and `model` start pins. Blank means the gateway's default text
model. The processor automation carries the user's "filing model" (a small fast model is
recommended, for example `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit` on Apple silicon); the reflect
automation and recall at standard and deep effort use the user's "answering model". The
automations take the models from the notebook settings when they are created.

### note-capture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start<br/>text, title?, occurred_at?, location?, source?,<br/>priority?, process_inline?, provider?, model?<br/>context.attachments] --> C[tool note_capture]
    C --> D{status}
    D -- duplicate --> M1[answer_user<br/>Already saved on date; link] --> E1[on_flow_end]
    D -- new --> Q[llm_call quick filing<br/>resp_schema QuickFiling]
    Q --> F[tool note_file<br/>title, kind, topics, urgency, language]
    F --> M2[answer_user<br/>Saved as kind 'title'. Related: ...]
    M2 --> I{process_inline?}
    I -- no --> E2[on_flow_end<br/>response, note_id, status=queued]
    I -- yes --> P[subflow note-process]
    P --> E3[on_flow_end<br/>response, note_id, status=processed, revision]
```

- `note_capture` reads attachments from the run's artifacts (inside the gateway, only
  `{"$artifact": id}` references resolved through the host's artifact store; local paths exist only
  in headless use with an allowed root), hashes bytes and text, stores the note and blobs, extracts
  text from documents and transcripts, returns `status` (`new` or `duplicate` for a retried
  idempotency key), the revisited notes (same words earlier) and similar notes (vector neighbours),
  the existing topics, and enqueues the note with the requested or default priority. The bound tool
  stamps `source.account` with the plane's account at bind time; `session_id` comes from a start
  pin; clients send an `idempotency_key`.
- Quick filing is one small-model call with the `QuickFiling` schema (below). It sees the note,
  the similar notes' titles and the existing topic list, and returns a title, a kind, topics, an
  urgency and the language. `note_file` stores them and maps urgency to queue priority.
- The answer is delivered twice: as an `answer_user` message as soon as it exists (clients that
  stream the ledger show it immediately) and as `output.response` when the run ends (clients
  that poll the run read it there). `process_inline` is the client's choice: the web app sends
  its "Instant linking" setting (`process_inline_default`, off by default); the watch always
  sends `false` and shows the filing answer.

### note-process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start note_id, provider?, model?] --> X[tool note_context<br/>text, extracted attachment text,<br/>similar notes, candidate entities,<br/>recent claims about them, topics]
    X --> E[llm_call extract<br/>resp_schema Extraction]
    E --> R[tool note_resolve_candidates<br/>per mention: alias, full-text, vector candidates]
    R --> J[llm_call link<br/>resp_schema Linking]
    J --> A[tool note_apply_revision]
    A --> Z[on_flow_end revision summary]
```

1. **Context** (`note_context`): what the notebook already knows that is relevant: the nearest
   notes, entities whose names or aliases appear in the text or whose embeddings are close,
   their current summaries and the active claims about them, the open tasks that mention them,
   and the topic vocabulary. This is the "look at the existing knowledge" step.
2. **Extract** (`Extraction` schema): summary, mentions (name, kind, aliases seen, role in the
   note), claims (subject, predicate, object, literal flag, certainty, stance, evidence excerpt,
   optional validity dates), tasks (opened, completed), time references, and topics. The prompt
   carries the predicate vocabulary from the AbstractSemantics registry and allows `ex:` for the
   rest.
3. **Resolve candidates** (`note_resolve_candidates`): for every mention, up to five existing
   entities with their kind, aliases, summary, last seen date and how they matched.
4. **Link** (`Linking` schema): the model decides, per mention, `reuse` (a candidate index),
   `create`, or `merge` (two candidate indexes); per claim, whether it `restates` an existing claim
   (reinforce), `refines` it (new claim, old stays active), `supersedes` it (close the old one) or
   `contradicts` it (both stay, marked disputed), naming the existing claim by its index in the
   packet; per task, open or close by index. The schema uses indexes and enumerations rather than
   free-form ids so that small models cannot invent identifiers; `note_apply_revision` rejects any
   reference outside the packet and downgrades it to `create` or `new` with a warning. The model
   also writes the revision summary and a one-sentence summary for each entity it creates and for
   each reused entity the note tells something new about.
5. **Apply** (`note_apply_revision`): writes the revision ops to the index and the triple store in
   one transaction per store, updates relations, topics, tasks, embeddings, and marks the note
   `processed`. The response lists created and merged entities, claims added and superseded, and
   any warnings (unknown predicates mapped to `ex:`, unresolved references).

Large notes: `note_context` splits texts beyond the model's budget into sections; `note-process`
loops over sections for extraction and merges mentions and claims before linking, so no text is
ever truncated.

### note-drain and the queue

The queue lives in the note index (`queue` table): `note_id, priority, enqueued_at, leased_by,
lease_until, attempts, last_error`. Ordering is `priority desc, occurred_at asc, size asc`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start max_items, budget_s, provider?, model?] --> L[tool note_queue_lease worker_id]
    L --> H{item?}
    H -- none --> Z[on_flow_end report]
    H -- yes --> P[subflow note-process]
    P --> K[tool note_queue_ack outcome, error?]
    K --> B{budget left?}
    B -- yes --> L
    B -- no --> Z
```

- A lease lasts 15 minutes; an expired lease is taken over by the next drain. Acknowledging a
  failure increments `attempts` and schedules a retry (after 1 minute, then after 10 minutes); the
  third failure sets the note to `failed`, visible in the web app's queue panel with the error,
  and offers a manual retry.
- **The processor automation.** `POST /api/gateway/note/processor/ensure` (the web app calls it
  when it opens and the automations are missing) creates two automations per user, idempotently: the processor
  (trigger `schedule@2` every `2m`, flow `note-drain`, `max_items = 20`, `budget_s = 90`) and the
  reflect automation (every `7d` by default, flow `note-reflect`), each with
  `_runtime.allowed_tools` listing the note tools. The processor's first drain runs at creation
  (an empty queue completes without a model call); the reflect automation's schedule starts one
  interval after creation (`start_at = now + every`), so opening an empty notebook never starts an
  answering-model call. "Reflect now" is the same `run_now` command sent to the reflect automation
  (`POST /api/gateway/automations/{reflect_id}/commands` with `{"command_id": "<uuid>", "type":
  "automation.run_now"}`).
  Automations run occurrences serially and coalesce missed ticks, which gives the queue exactly
  the eventual, ordered consistency it needs without a gateway worker. "Process now" sends the
  automation's `run_now` command; a `409 automation_busy` answer means a drain is already running
  and the queue panel says so. Steady-state throughput is at most `max_items` per interval.
- **No approval waits.** Inside the gateway the note tools are added to the tool approval
  auto-approve set when the runtime is built, so a capture never parks on a tool-approval wait.
- **Priority**: `3` urgent and `2` high come from the quick filing step (tasks with deadlines,
  warnings, anything the user marks urgent); `1` normal is the default for interactive capture;
  `0` bulk is used by importers so that live notes always go first.
- **Concurrency**: one occurrence at a time per user; the gateway's own runner limits concurrent
  ticks across users. Local models serve requests one at a time, so serial processing is also
  the fastest total throughput on a single machine.

### note-recall

`note-recall` also serves the `abstractcode.agent.v1` chat contract: it accepts `prompt` as an
alias of `question` and always returns the answer text on the `response` output pin next to the
structured pins, so a chat client that polls `output.response` shows the answer.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start question or prompt, effort, as_of?, since?, until?,<br/>entities?, topics?, provider?, model?] --> Q[tool note_search quick]
    Q --> E{effort}
    E -- quick --> Z1[on_flow_end response, hits]
    E -- standard --> X[tool note_expand<br/>entity cards as_of, claims timeline,<br/>neighbours, then-vs-now pairs]
    X --> L[llm_call synthesize<br/>resp_schema Answer]
    L --> Z2[on_flow_end response, answer, evidence, follow_ups]
    E -- deep --> M[subflow note-mine] --> Z3[on_flow_end answer, dossier_note_id]
```

The `Answer` schema returns the answer text with inline citations `[nt_...]`, the evidence list,
what changed over time about the subject (earliest stance, latest stance, turning points with
note ids), open loops related to the question, and suggested follow-up questions. Clients render
citations as links to notes.

### note-mine (deep)

1. `llm_call plan` (`MiningPlan` schema): sub-questions, time slices, entities to trace,
   contradictions to test, a budget of search rounds.
2. Loop over the plan: `note_search` and `note_entity` for each item, `llm_call findings` per
   slice (`SliceFindings` schema: facts with citations, changes, gaps).
3. `llm_call dossier` (`Dossier` schema): narrative, timeline of the subject, how the view evolved,
   contradictions, forgotten items worth revisiting, suggestions, and a confidence statement.
4. `note_insight_write` stores the dossier as a `synthesis` note with provenance (the run id,
   the evidence notes, the entities), so the result is itself searchable and revisitable.

### note-reflect

Runs from a scheduled automation (default weekly, configurable); its first occurrence is one
interval after the automation is created, and "Reflect now" (`automation.run_now`) runs it at once.
A failed occurrence is retried by the automation (up to 3 attempts). Deterministic tools produce
candidates; the model judges and writes:

| Tool | Candidates |
|---|---|
| `note_open_loops` | open tasks older than N days, questions never answered |
| `note_contradictions` | disputed claim pairs, single-valued predicates with several active objects |
| `note_resurface` | entities and topics active before but silent for N days that relate to recent notes |
| `note_anniversaries` | notes from the same day in previous months or years |

`llm_call reflect` (`Reflections` schema) selects what deserves attention and writes each item
as an `insight` note (`warning`, `reminder`, `connection`, `contradiction`, `evolution`). The
web app's Remember view and the watch's Today screen show unacknowledged insights.

## Structured output schemas

All schemas are JSON Schema objects attached as `resp_schema`; the runtime builds pydantic
models from them and repairs invalid output. Python mirrors live in `abstractnote.process.schemas`.

**QuickFiling**

```json
{"title": "string (<= 80 chars)", "kind": "idea|task|decision|fact|event|question|reflection|reference|log|conversation|personal",
 "topics": ["string, prefer existing topics, at most 4"], "urgency": "bulk|normal|high|urgent",
 "language": "BCP-47", "one_line": "string"}
```

**Extraction**

```json
{"summary": "1-3 sentences",
 "mentions": [{"ref": "m1", "name": "string", "kind": "person|org|project|concept|place|event|artifact|software|thing",
               "aliases": ["as written in the note"], "role": "what the note says about it, one phrase"}],
 "claims": [{"subject": "m1", "predicate": "CURIE from the vocabulary or ex:snake_case", "object": "m2 or literal",
             "object_is_literal": false, "certainty": "stated|probable|possible|reported|disputed",
             "stance": "assert|revise|retract", "evidence": "verbatim excerpt", "valid_from": "ISO or null", "valid_until": "ISO or null"}],
 "tasks": [{"text": "string", "status": "open|done", "due": "ISO or null"}],
 "time_refs": [{"text": "string", "iso": "ISO or null"}],
 "topics": ["string"]}
```

**Linking** (indexes refer to the candidate lists in the context packet; enumerations are JSON
Schema enums)

```json
{"mentions": [{"ref": "m1", "decision": "reuse|create|merge|unsure", "candidate": 0,
               "merge_candidates": [0, 1], "name": "preferred name", "kind": "person|org|project|concept|place|event|artifact|software|thing",
               "aliases": ["..."], "summary": "one sentence; required for create and unsure, and for a reused entity this note tells something new about; otherwise null", "reason": "short"}],
 "claims": [{"index": 0, "relation_to_existing": "new|restates|refines|supersedes|contradicts",
             "existing": 0, "reason": "short"}],
 "tasks": [{"index": 0, "closes_open_task": 0}],
 "revision_summary": "one sentence"}
```

**Answer**, **MiningPlan**, **SliceFindings**, **Dossier**, **Reflections**: see
`abstractnote.process.schemas`; each is documented inline with the fields listed above.

## Prompts

Prompts are Markdown files under `src/abstractnote/process/prompts/` rendered with the context
packet. Rules that every prompt states:

- Use only the note and the provided context; never invent entities or dates.
- Prefer reusing an existing entity when the candidate list contains it; create sparingly.
- Keep names as written by the author; put variants in aliases.
- Quote evidence verbatim; one claim per statement; no inferred hierarchy.
- When unsure whether two things are the same, say `unsure` (treated as `create` plus a
  `skos:closeMatch` claim for later consolidation) rather than guessing.
- Output JSON only, matching the schema.

The predicate vocabulary is loaded from the AbstractSemantics registry at build time and listed
in the extraction prompt with one-line glosses. Predicates outside it are accepted as
`ex:snake_case` and reported in the revision warnings so the vocabulary can grow deliberately.

## Headless execution

`abstractnote process --local --notebook DIR --provider mlx --model <id>` runs `note-drain` without a gateway:
the same compiled flows on a local `Runtime` with real effect handlers (AbstractCore model calls,
the note tools bound to a local notebook directory). This is how the importers are processed in
bulk, how the test suite exercises the flows with a scripted model, and how you can run the
processor on a machine that is not the gateway host. The recipe follows AbstractRuntime's
`test_kg_learn_and_recall_contract` harness (`compile_visualflow_tree`, `WorkflowRegistry`,
`build_effect_handlers`, drive subflow waits).

---

## docs/remembering.md

# Remembering

Search engines answer queries. Memory answers cues. AbstractNote's recall is built around the
ways people (and agents) actually try to remember, and around how much effort they are willing
to spend. This page explains the design that the **Remember** view, the recall tools and the
`note-recall` flow implement.

## How we remember

| Cue | What you have | What you want | AbstractNote answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time | "around the release in September", "last winter" | what was going on then | the day and period views: notes, revisions, entities touched, what you believed then |
| Person or thing | "Dana", "the LUT project" | everything you know, and how it changed | the entity card as of a moment, the claims timeline, then-versus-now |
| Fragment | three words you are sure were in the note | the note | quick recall: full-text plus vector, grouped by entity and date |
| Feeling or shape | "that idea I was excited about", "a warning I wrote myself" | the note or the insight | kinds and topics as filters, insights as first-class notes |
| Association | "it came up together with X" | the neighbours | graph expansion from the hits, relations with first and last seen |
| Absence | "did I ever decide this?" "what have I dropped?" | the gap | open loops, contradictions, resurfacing, the reflect insights |
| Evolution | "what did I used to think?" | the arc | earliest stance, latest stance, turning points with the notes that caused them |

Agents have the same needs with different vocabulary: an agent asked to continue work needs the
latest decision and the reason it changed; an agent starting a task needs the entities involved
and their current state; an agent writing a report needs the timeline with citations. The same
structures serve both, which is why every answer is returned as structured JSON with note ids as
citations, and the web app renders that JSON.

## Effort levels

| Level | Budget | What runs | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| **quick** | under a second, no model | full-text (FTS5, BM25) plus vector search over notes, entities and claims; grouping by entity and month; facets | hits with excerpts, matched entities, matched claims, facets |
| **standard** | seconds, one model call | quick retrieval, then graph expansion (entity cards as of the requested moment, claim timelines, neighbours, then-versus-now pairs), then one synthesis | an answer with citations, the evidence, the evolution summary, open loops, follow-ups |
| **deep** | minutes, several model calls, runs in the background | a mining plan (sub-questions, time slices, entities, contradictions), several retrieval rounds with findings per slice, a dossier | the dossier as an answer and as a stored `synthesis` note; the web app and the watch show it when it is ready |

The level is a parameter everywhere: the Remember view has an effort dial, the watch asks at
standard by default, agents pass it explicitly, and the CLI takes `--effort`. A deep search is
never blocking: the run starts, the client gets a run id, and the dossier appears as an insight.

## The Remember view

The Remember view opens on what changed and lets you dig from there. Its first screen (since you
last looked beside the cue cards, then the ask bar) fits a 1280x800 window; the rest follows below.

1. **Since you last looked** (the default screen): what the notebook learned since your last
   visit: new entities, beliefs that were replaced ("Replaced") or withdrawn ("Withdrawn"), loops
   that closed, insights, notes that failed to process. It is a system-time delta from a cursor, so it is the same call an agent
   makes at the start of every session (`GET /note/changes?since=`). Each item opens its subject.
   The web app shows it as a compact list, one line per change with a word for its kind
   (Replaced, Withdrawn, Closed, Needs attention, New); new notes fold into one line that opens.
2. **Cue cards**: a few prompts the reflect flow generated from the graph, each answerable by
   adding a note: a person who went quiet, a decision that is a year old, a task mentioned three
   times and never closed. Answering a cue writes a note linked to its subject; the answered
   rate is the measure of whether the cards are worth showing. Cue cards are insights, so an
   insight shown as a cue is not repeated under Revisit or in the delta. Every cue and insight has
   **Why this surfaced**: its kind in plain words (a reminder, a connection, a contradiction, an
   evolution, ...) and the notes it is based on.
3. **The ask bar** with the effort dial and cue chips: *when* (a date, a range, "around" an
   entity's active period), *who/what* (entities), *kind* (idea, decision, task, ...), *topic*.
   Typing shows quick results immediately; with Quick chosen there is no Ask button, the
   matching notes follow the typing. Ask runs standard or deep and shows its steps as they happen
   (searched your notes, looked closer at what they connect, wrote the answer). An answer has three
   layers, each named and drawn differently: the **Synthesis** (what the selected notes suggest,
   with citations), the **Original** (the notes it rests on, quoted as you wrote them) and the
   **Interpretation** (what the notebook understood: how it changed, what is still open). Each
   citation opens the note with its attachments and the revision it caused. "Save this answer"
   turns it into a note with provenance; the note dialog shows such notes as synthesis, never as
   something you wrote.
4. **Then versus now**: for an entity or for a relationship between two entities, the earliest
   and the latest summary side by side, with the turning points between them listed with their
   notes. Cached per revision; the fastest way to see how your understanding of a person, a
   project, an idea or a link evolved.
5. **Why do I believe this**: every claim, and every sentence of an answer, opens its evidence
   chain: the claim, what it superseded or was superseded by, the notes, the attachment excerpt.
   One tap says "this is wrong" and writes a retract revision with your account as the source.
6. **Revisit**: open loops with a close action, unread insights, "on this day" notes, entities
   that went silent but relate to what you added this week, contradictions awaiting a decision.
7. **To review** (only when there is something, `GET /note/review`): what the notebook decided
   on its own, each with why, the two sides, the notes behind them and its own actions. A merge it
   made: **Keep** (recorded for your account, `POST /note/review/{id}/confirm`) or **Undo the
   match** (separates them again; the joined entry's own name and notes come from
   `GET /note/entities/{id}?as_merged=true`). A close match it was unsure about: **Same** (joins
   them) or **Not the same** (withdraws the close match). Two notes that disagree: say which one is
   wrong (withdraws that statement).

Each entity card carries a small activity sparkline. A multi-lane time river is a candidate for
a later version once real notebooks show which lanes deserve a lane; the time scrubber in the
Explore view already covers "what did this look like then".

## The Explore view (the graph)

- **Focus and depth**: pick one or several entities; see their neighbourhood up to depth three,
  edges labelled by predicate with first and last seen dates and counts.
- **Picture or List**: the same connections drawn, or as a readable table (from, link, to, since,
  believed or no longer believed); each row opens the link's history or the entity.
- **Time scrubber and date field**: moving the slider or choosing a date changes `as_of` (the date
  field reaches any day without dragging). Beside it, **True then** reads the date as what your
  notes said was true then (`at`); **Saved by then** reads it as what the notebook held on that
  date (`as_received`: only notes received by then), so a June note imported in October is absent
  from a September snapshot. The layout stays where it is: entities and edges that did not exist yet fade
  out, superseded claims show as dashed; the entity card shows the beliefs at that moment. An edge
  opens the relation timeline between its two entities.
- **Day page**: "what happened on day X": notes captured, revisions applied with their one-line
  summaries, entities created or merged, claims superseded.
- **Entity page** (the topic portrait): name, aliases and activity, then five tabs. **How it
  evolved** comes first: the first note, the dated views from the summary history (earlier view,
  refined, latest expressed view) and the changes between them (a belief replaced or withdrawn),
  oldest first, each opening its note or its evidence; with a date chosen, the milestones after it
  stay in place, faded. Then **Changes** (what you believe or believed then, then-versus-now),
  **Open actions**, **Sources** (the notes) and **Links** (relations). An entity that absorbed
  others names them ("Includes Dana R. (1 note)", from each entry's own record). An entity asked
  for at a date before it existed says so.

## The Capture view

A stream of your notes as you wrote them, with the composer at the bottom. You type or paste,
attach files (images show a preview), drop images, or dictate; Enter saves and Shift+Enter starts
a new line; with your permission the browser attaches your location. Under each note one short
acknowledgement shows one state at a time, as a word and a symbol: **Sending**, **Received**,
**Organizing**, then **Organized** or **Needs attention**. Organized reads like "Added to #lut ·
event · 2 links" and opens on what was filed: the note's title, topics, linked entities, when you
said the same thing before, and what it changed. Until the note is organized the details show
the notebook's reply. With "Instant linking" on (Settings) the note is processed right away;
otherwise the app re-reads the note until it is. Nothing uses system vocabulary: no run ids, no
ledger, no gateway.

## For agents and entities

- `note_changes` (since you last looked) is the first call of a session; `note_search` at quick
  effort is cheap enough to call before every task.
- `note-recall` at standard effort returns the latest decision and why it changed, with
  citations, in one call; agents should quote the note ids in their own outputs so provenance
  survives.
- Deep recall returns a dossier note id; an agent can wait for the run or come back later.
- Agents capture notes through the same `note-capture` flow with `source.client = "agent"` and
  `source.author = <agent name>`, so the notebook records who learned what and when.

---

## docs/clients.md

# Clients

AbstractNote ships a web app and an Apple Watch app, and reserves the structure for an iPhone
app. All clients are thin: the gateway owns authentication, execution and state. They share one
contract: sign in to a gateway, start the `note-capture` and `note-recall` flows with the runs
API, read the note API for views, and never send user, tenant or runtime identifiers.

## Sign-in and isolation

- A client signs in with a gateway account token (`Authorization: Bearer`) verified against
  `GET /api/gateway/me`, or with an emailed one-time code (`POST /session/recovery/request`, then
  `/redeem`) that yields a session id and CSRF token sent as headers on later requests.
- Sign-out clears the stored credential locally and, for sessions, calls
  `POST /session/logout`. A `401` on any call returns the client to sign-in.
- The gateway routes every request to the caller's own data plane, so one gateway serves many
  users and each sees only their own notebook. Use a dedicated `user`-role account per person or
  device; never an admin token.
- Credential storage on Apple clients: a file in the app container protected with Data
  Protection (`completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication`), not the OS keychain, following the
  framework's file-sealed secrets rule. The gateway address is stored next to it. This choice is
  proposed and awaits a ruling ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-apple-client-credential-storage.md)).

## Web app (`web/`)

- npm package `@abstractframework/note`, built with Vite, React and TypeScript, using
  `@abstractframework/ui-kit`, `@abstractframework/panel-chat` and `@abstractframework/app-server`
  from the npm registry with semver ranges.
- Served by the gateway at `/apps/note/` through the app proxy. The app's Node server answers the
  mount header, relays `/api/*` to the gateway with the session cookie, binds `127.0.0.1`, and
  uses relative URLs and the shared shell, as the app-server contract requires.
- Three views, in the tab order **Capture**, **Remember**, **Explore** (the graph; its route stays
  `#/graph`) (see [remembering.md](remembering.md)), plus a small **Settings** drawer (filing model, answering model, inline processing, reflect schedule,
  location, queue status with retry, appearance, sign-out). Location is off until you turn on the
  Location switch in Settings (kept per browser, and offered only on a secure page); Capture then
  attaches it to notes.
- Theming uses ui-kit tokens only, so every kit theme works; tested on default-dark, observer-night
  and solarized-light at 1280 and 400 px. The framework look comes from derivations of those
  tokens: on dark themes the page colour is deepened toward near-black (relative colour of
  `--bg-primary`; light themes keep theirs), fine borders, Inter when installed (else the kit
  font), and an indigo, cyan and mint accent mixed from `--info`, `--accent` and `--success` used
  for state and emphasis only. Primary actions keep the theme's `--accent`.
- Accessibility: text follows the appearance text size (`--font-scale`, graph labels included);
  focus rings are always visible; every state is a word and a symbol, never colour alone (capture
  states, believed / no longer believed, the answer's three layers); every graph has a readable
  relationship list (Explore, List); dates are chosen with a date field, never only by dragging;
  reduced motion turns animation off.
- Registered by the AbstractGateway integration in the gateway's app catalog, tray, web console
  and terminal console as `note` (port 3006, cookie prefix `abstractnote`, page title
  `AbstractNote`, command `abstractnote-web`).

Development: `npm install`, then `npm run dev -- --gateway-url <url>` serves the app against a
gateway, and `npm run dev:mock` against a built-in sample notebook; `npm run build` produces
`dist/`; `node bin/cli.js --port 3006 --gateway-url
http://127.0.0.1:8080` runs the production server the way the gateway launches it.

## Apple Watch app (`watch/apple/`)

- XcodeGen project `project.yml`: target `AbstractNoteWatch` (watchOS 26, bundle id
  `ai.abstractframework.note.watch`), an empty iOS container `AbstractNote`
  (`ai.abstractframework.note`) for App Store packaging, a UI test target, Swift 6 with strict
  concurrency. `WKWatchOnly` is set; the app runs independently of a phone.
- Swift package `Packages/AbstractGatewayClient`: the gateway client (credential, sign-in,
  requests with read retries, run start and polling, note API reads) and a
  mock client for previews and screenshots. It starts as a documented snapshot of the
  AbstractAssistant watch client (`SNAPSHOT.json` records the source and hashes) and adds the
  note endpoints; the two clients are candidates for a shared package once their APIs settle.
- Screens:
  - **Note**: a text field (watchOS dictation and scribble come free with it) and a Send button at
    the bottom; after sending, the filing answer ("Saved as idea 'LUT budget'. Related: Dana,
    LUT.") with a Done button. Location is attached when the user allowed it. Each send carries a
    fresh idempotency key so a radio retry never duplicates a note.
  - **Ask**: dictate a question, see the standard-effort answer with the evidence titles; "Dig
    deeper" starts a deep recall and the result shows in Today when ready.
  - **Today**: what changed since you last looked, unacknowledged insights, open loops, cue
    cards and on-this-day notes; tap to acknowledge, close, or add a note about it.
  - **Settings**: the server and account, the Place switch (location), About, Sign out.
- Build and test: `scripts/build.sh` (XcodeGen, `swift test`, simulator build, screenshots of
  every screen with the mock client), `scripts/deploy-watch.sh` (signed build and install on a
  paired watch through `devicectl`, gateway and token passed as launch arguments), and a GitHub
  workflow (`.github/workflows/watch.yml`) that builds and tests on every change to `watch/apple/`.
- End-user copy rules: plain verbs, one-sentence errors, actions at the bottom, no system
  vocabulary, VoiceOver labels on every control, no state shown by colour alone, nothing
  consequential without a tap.

## iPhone app (`phone/iphone/`)

Planned. The folder holds the plan: the same package layout as the watch with a richer Capture
(camera, files, voice memos), the full Graph and Remember views, and share-sheet capture from
other apps. The bundle id reserved is `ai.abstractframework.note.iphone`, following the
AbstractAssistant precedent of watch-only plus separate iPhone app; if the watch app should
later become a companion of the iPhone app, the bundle parentage changes before the first
public release of either.

## CLI and agents

The `abstractnote` CLI is a headless tool on a notebook directory (`--notebook DIR`);
`--gateway URL --token T` is reserved for a client mode that is not available in this version.
Agents and entities running inside the same gateway call the note tools directly; agents
elsewhere use the runs API like any client.

---

## docs/importers.md

# Importers

Importers turn existing corpora into notes with faithful history time and provenance. They write
notes directly into a notebook at bulk priority (`0`) and let the processor understand them in
the background, so a large import never delays live notes. Every imported note keeps a `source`
object that points back to the exact origin, and re-running an import is idempotent because note
ids derive from the source key.

| Importer | Command | One note per | `occurred_at` | `source.origin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code sessions | `abstractnote import claude-sessions DIR` | human-typed prompt, with the final assistant text of that turn as the outcome; one note per session summary (title, compaction and away summaries); one note per subagent run (its brief and its last report); one note per curated memory file | the record timestamp | `{session_id, uuid, prompt_id, cwd, git_branch, model, file, line}` |
| Agora hub | `abstractnote import agora DB` | recorded decision (`store decision:*`), claim and work entry, resolved or answered thread (root plus replies), operator message | `created_at` | `{message_id, channel, seq, sender, reply_to, status, hash}` |
| Markdown tree | `abstractnote import markdown DIR` | file (ADRs, backlog items, notes), with front-matter and headings kept | front-matter dates, else the first git commit date, else the file date | `{repo, path, blob_sha, commit}` |
| Files | `abstractnote import files PATH...` | file (documents, images, audio, video, logs) | file date or EXIF | `{path, sha256}` |

Rules shared by all importers:

- Skip machine noise: tool results, hook output, system reminders, presence and silence alerts,
  file-change notices. Keep what a person or an agent wrote on purpose.
- Keep whole texts. Large texts are sectioned at processing time, never truncated.
- Attach images by hash and type; do not inline bytes into notes.
- Mark the author: `source.author` is the account name, the agent seat, or the model name.
- Private content stays in the notebook; importers never post or copy anything outside it.
- Report counts (notes created, duplicates skipped, attachments stored) and the time range covered.

Every importer takes `--notebook DIR`, `--since`, `--until` and `--dry-run` (count only, write
nothing) and prints a counts report as JSON; the full flag list is in [api.md](api.md#cli). A
notebook pinned to an embedding server is opened with the same `--embed-base-url` and
`--embed-model` that `capture` and `process` take
([troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md#this-notebooks-vectors-were-made-with-the-embedding-model-)).

Processing an import runs through the same `note-process` flow as live notes. Expect roughly two
model calls per note; with a small local model this is a few seconds per note, so a corpus of a
few thousand notes takes hours. Run `abstractnote process --local` on the machine that holds the
model, or let the gateway's processor automation drain the queue over time.

---

## CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to AbstractNote

Thank you for helping. This page covers the development setup, the tests, the generated flows and
the rules that keep the product consistent. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)
first; the HTTP, tool and CLI contracts are in [docs/api.md](docs/api.md), and the design
decisions in [docs/adr/](docs/adr/README.md).

## Development environment

Clone the framework packages next to this repository (the AbstractFramework `scripts/clone.sh`
does this) and install them editable into one virtual environment, so changes in a sibling
package are picked up without a release:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractsemantics -e ../abstractcore -e ../abstractruntime \
                      -e ../abstractmemory       # with close_assertion
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractgateway      # the abstractnote-seam branch, for gateway work
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Never install framework packages from PyPI into this environment when a sibling checkout exists:
the released versions lack the changes AbstractNote depends on.

## Tests

```sh
.venv/bin/pytest -q                                # the Python suite (scripted models, no weights)
.venv/bin/python -m abstractnote.flows.build --check
cd web && npm install && npm test && npm run build # web app: vitest, type check, build
cd watch/apple && scripts/build.sh                 # watch app: package tests, simulator build, screenshots
```

- Python tests use scripted models and the built-in hashing embedder; they never load a model.
  The gateway tests run when `abstractgateway` is installed and are skipped otherwise.
- A test that spawns processes must give them a scratch `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `HF_HOME`.
- A scratch gateway for manual checks: `scripts/hermetic_gateway.sh start|status|stop` (ports
  18800-18899, scratch data directory, scripted model); see
  [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md#try-it-on-a-private-scratch-gateway).
- Every check you add must fail when the thing it checks is removed. Delete it once and watch the
  test go red.

## Flows

The flow JSON in `src/abstractnote/flows/json/` is generated. Edit the generator
(`src/abstractnote/flows/build.py`, `graph.py`), the prompts (`src/abstractnote/process/prompts/`)
or the schemas (`src/abstractnote/process/schemas.py`), then regenerate and commit the JSON:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m abstractnote.flows.build          # write
.venv/bin/python -m abstractnote.flows.build --check  # exit 1 when the JSON is stale
.venv/bin/abstractnote bundle --out dist/             # pack abstractnote@<version>.flow
```

Flows use catalog node types only. Every tool call is visible as its own nodes, and a tool's
failure ends the run with the tool's own sentence.

## Rules

- **No text heuristics for meaning.** Regular expressions or keyword lists never decide identity,
  intent or meaning. Deterministic code produces exact hashes and candidates; models decide
  ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-models-decide-identity-no-text-heuristics.md)).
- **Tools stay bookkeeping.** Judgement lives in `llm_call` nodes with structured output; note
  tools hash, store, look up and apply ([ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-flows-carry-cognition-tools-carry-bookkeeping.md)).
  Tools raise `ValueError` with one plain sentence on bad input and never log secrets.
- **Isolation.** Clients never send user, tenant or runtime identifiers; inside a gateway, tools
  never accept filesystem paths.
- **End-user copy.** In the web and watch apps: plain verbs; one-sentence errors; no system words
  such as ledger, run, gateway, workflow, record, and no ids; switches are labelled by the feature
  they control; actions sit at the bottom; nothing consequential happens without a tap. The web
  app's `test/copy.test.ts` checks the view strings.
- **Docs follow the code.** When you change behaviour, update the page that owns it (see
  [docs/README.md](docs/README.md)) and regenerate `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` in the same
  change. User-visible changes go in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Pull requests

Keep a pull request to one concern, include the tests that prove it, and say in the description
which documents changed. Report security issues privately as described in
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not in a pull request or issue.

---

## SECURITY.md

# Security Policy

AbstractNote keeps personal notes, files and the knowledge drawn from them. Please report
vulnerabilities privately so they can be fixed before public disclosure.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do **not** open a public issue for a security report. Use GitHub's private **Report a
vulnerability** form on the AbstractNote repository, or write to contact@abstractcore.ai.

Please include:

- a description of the issue and its impact;
- the affected component (core library, flows, gateway integration, web app, watch app, importers)
  and file paths if known;
- steps to reproduce or a minimal proof of concept;
- the version (`abstractnote status` shows it) and your environment;
- a suggested fix, if you have one.

We acknowledge reports as promptly as we can and agree a disclosure timeline with you.

## Supported versions

AbstractNote is in development (0.1.0, not yet published). Security fixes go to the `main`
branch.

## Security model

These are the guarantees the design makes; a way around any of them is a vulnerability.

- **Per-user isolation.** Inside AbstractGateway every request is authenticated by the gateway
  and routed to the caller's own data plane; the notebook lives under that plane. Clients never
  send user, tenant or runtime identifiers, and an id from another notebook answers 404.
- **No filesystem paths inside the gateway.** The note tools read attachments only from files
  uploaded through the gateway (`{"$artifact": id}` from the host's artifact store). A path in a
  capture is refused. Headless use accepts paths only inside a folder the caller allows
  explicitly.
- **Auto-approved tools touch only your notebook.** The note tools are auto-approved because each
  one is bound to the caller's notebook and to nothing else.
- **Accounts.** Clients sign in with a `user` account token or an emailed one-time code; admin
  tokens are not meant for clients. The note tools never print or log secrets.
- **Importers read, never write, their sources.** The agora importer opens the hub database
  read-only; importers copy nothing outside the notebook.
- **Apple clients** keep the sign-in in one protected file in the app container (Data Protection,
  excluded from backup, deleted on sign-out), not in the OS keychain. This storage is proposed and
  awaits a ruling ([ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-apple-client-credential-storage.md)).

## What you should protect

- The notebook is plain SQLite files and attachment blobs on disk, not encrypted by AbstractNote.
  Protect the gateway's data directory (or your `--notebook` directory) with the operating
  system's file permissions and disk encryption.
- Imports can bring private material (sessions, messages, documents) into a notebook. Import
  only what the notebook's owner may hold.

---

## CHANGELOG.md

# Changelog

All notable user-visible changes to AbstractNote are listed here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.1.0] - Unreleased

The first version. It is installed from source; PyPI, npm and App Store publication are pending.

### Added

- **Notebook**: notes with history time, place and provenance; attachments stored once per
  content; idempotent capture (a retried send answers `duplicate`); notes that repeat or resemble
  earlier ones are linked to them as revisits.
- **Understanding**: quick filing (title, kind, topics, urgency, language), then extraction,
  candidate lookup and model-decided linking of entities, claims and tasks, applied as revisions
  to a note index and an AbstractMemory triple store. Facts are superseded, never overwritten;
  the graph and the beliefs at any past moment can be read back.
- **Queue**: priorities (urgent, high, normal, bulk), leases, retries after one and ten minutes,
  failed notes visible with their error and a retry action.
- **Flows**: `note-capture`, `note-process`, `note-drain`, `note-recall`, `note-mine` and
  `note-reflect` in the `abstractnote` bundle, editable in the Flow editor and runnable
  headlessly; `note-recall` also answers the `abstractcode.agent.v1` chat contract.
- **Recall**: quick (full-text plus vector, no model), standard (graph expansion and one cited
  synthesis), deep (a stored dossier); since-you-last-looked changes, cue cards, entity cards as
  of a moment, then-versus-now, relation timelines, evidence chains, day and timeline views.
- **Reflection**: open loops, contradictions, resurfacing and anniversaries turned into insights
  on a schedule; the first one runs a full interval after the notebook is set up (opening an
  empty notebook never starts a model), or at once with "Reflect now".
- **User actions**: close a task, retract a claim, undo a merge, acknowledge an insight, archive
  a note; each one is a revision with the account as its source. A claim you retract was never
  true; "since you last looked" lists it as withdrawn, in plain words.
- **Gateway integration** (with the AbstractGateway integration): per-user note tools,
  auto-approved; the note read API under `/api/gateway/note`; the processor and reflect
  automations through `POST /note/processor/ensure`; the Note app in the gateway's app catalog.
- **Web app** `@abstractframework/note`: Capture, Graph, Remember and Settings.
- **Apple Watch app**: Note, Ask, Today and Settings; watch-only, watchOS 26 or later.
- **Command line** `abstractnote`: capture, search, entity, day, status, changes, rebuild,
  process, bundle and import, on a notebook directory.
- **Importers**: Claude Code sessions, an agora hub database (read-only), Markdown trees and
  files, with original dates, provenance and `--dry-run` counts.

### Requirements

- An AbstractMemory release with `close_assertion`, and an AbstractGateway release with the
  AbstractNote integration, for the gateway path.

---
